- Semantic invariant: Animal bodies and earth are acted upon by force that stirs, opens, or scores material.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:67-71 supplies the cow, slaughter, stirred soil, field, and watering operations.
- Surprising reach: The same opening operation can cut an animal throat, score earth, or form a water-course.

#### Subchannel A. Bovine traction and field work
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A bovine body provides force that disturbs soil, prepares a field, and serves cultivation.
- Active motifs: cattle as the working animal (`ب ق ر:B001/m01`); bull as male bovine (`ث و ر:B004/m01`); stirring matter from its place (`ث و ر:B002/m01`); sowing seed and cultivating (`ح ر ث:B002/m01`); trampled or worked ground (`ح ر ث:B008/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:67-71 `بَقَرَة`; 2:71 `تُثِير`, `حَرْث`.
- Synthesis: Animal, motive force, disturbed soil, sowing, and worn ground form a compact agricultural operation rather than a generic animal motif.

#### Subchannel B. Incision and made channels
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Cutting opens a body or ground and produces a passage through which blood or water can move.
- Active motifs: opening the throat in slaughter (`ذ ب ح:B001/m01`); water channels incised in earth (`ذ ب ح:B004/m01`); splitting something open (`ب ق ر:B002/m01`); digging and scoring ground (`ب ق ر:B003/m01`); allotted irrigation channel (`س ق ي:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:67, 2:71 `تَذْبَحُوا`, `ذَبَحُوا`; 2:67-71 `بَقَرَة`; 2:71 `تَسْقِي`.
- Synthesis: The channel joins distinct cutting operations through a shared mechanism: an incision changes a closed surface into a conduit.

### 9. P5 (2:75-86) - Bonds that obligate and protect
- Semantic invariant: A durable social bond places its members under preserved obligation, mutual support, and care.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:80, 2:83-85 name covenant, parents, kin, orphans, mutual aid, and violated communal obligations.
- Surprising reach: Covenant can be imaged as a protective compact, while orphanhood exposes what happens when the expected stream of care is cut or delayed.

#### Subchannel A. Covenant as protected affiliation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Parties enter a preserved compact and become joined by support, loyalty, kinship, emancipation, or protected residence.
- Active motifs: compact and covenant (`ر ب ب:B011/m01`); preserved pact that secures its holder (`ع ه د:B003/m01`); loving support and alliance (`و ل ي:B004/m01`); affiliation by kinship, emancipation, or clientage (`و ل ي:B005/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:76 `رَبِّ`; 2:80 `عَهْدًا`; 2:83 `تَوَلَّيْتُم`.
- Synthesis: The compact is not only a spoken promise. It creates an affiliation whose practical expression is protection and mutual backing.

#### Subchannel B. Kinship and interrupted care
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Parents and kin sustain dependents, while orphanhood marks severance from a guardian and the slowing of expected kindness.
- Active motifs: mother as bearer and nurturer (`ء م م:B001/m01`); parents through procreation (`و ل د:B002/m01`); blood kinship (`ق ر ب:B003/m01`); child cut off from a guardian (`ي ت م:B001/m01`); kindness delayed from an orphan (`ي ت م:B004/m01`); foster-child relation (`ر ب ب:B005/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:78 `أُمِّيُّون`; 2:83 `وَالِدَيْن`, `قُرْبَى`, `يَتَامَى`; 2:76 `رَبِّ`.
- Synthesis: The scene maps a care network from parent and kin to fosterage. Orphanhood is its structural negative: the dependent remains while the responsible caregiver is absent or slow to act.

### 10. P5 (2:75-86) - Recorded words in exchange
- Semantic invariant: Words and writings become accountable objects that hands produce, claim, transfer, and exchange for value.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:78-81 places book, writing, hands, speech, price, acquisition, and earnings in one transactional discourse.
- Surprising reach: Authorship is treated as manual production, while a doctrinal claim can function like merchandise offered for a return.

#### Subchannel A. Hand-produced record and claim
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Hands compose a written object, speech attributes a claim to it, and the producer acquires consequences through the act.
- Active motifs: ordered letters and written object (`ك ت ب:B002/m01`); spoken utterance (`ق و ل:B001/m01`); saying or attributing what was not (`ق و ل:B005/m01`); what hands have earned (`ي د ي:B009/m01`); causing another to acquire good or wealth (`ك س ب:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:79 `يَكْتُبُون`, `كِتَاب`, `كَتَبَتْ`, `يَقُولُون`, `أَيْدِيهِم`, `يَكْسِبُون`; 2:81 `كَسَبَ`.
- Synthesis: Record, utterance, manual authorship, and acquired consequence form a production chain in which text is made and then socially asserted.

#### Subchannel B. Acquisition, handover, and price
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An object or position is acquired through exchange, passed by hand, and measured by a price.
- Active motifs: taking for oneself and acquiring (`ء خ ذ:B010/m01`); hand as the instrument of transfer (`ي د ي:B007/m01`); reciprocal buying and selling (`ش ر ي:B001/m01`); value received in exchange (`ث م ن:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:79 `يَشْتَرُون`, `ثَمَنًا`, `أَيْدِيهِم`; 2:80, 2:83-84 `اتَّخَذْتُم`, `أَخَذْنَا`; 2:86 `اشْتَرَوُا`.
- Synthesis: Acquisition is resolved into its transactional parts: taking, manual conveyance, reciprocal exchange, and valuation.

### 11. P6 (2:87-103) - Message reception and relay
- Semantic invariant: A message travels through voiced transmission, attentive reception, tracking, and recognition.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:87-93 and 2:97-102 repeatedly present messengers, hearing, following, recitation, recognition, and transmitted reports.
- Surprising reach: Following a messenger becomes literally following an observable trace, while recitation can be heard as one voice answering another.

#### Subchannel A. Voiced relay
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: One voice raises and sends a signal, another voice follows it, and an ear receives or admits it.
- Active motifs: hearing sound (`س م ع:B001/m01`); making another hear (`س م ع:B004/m01`); listening with acceptance (`ء ذ ن:B002/m01`); one voice following another (`ت ل و:B007/m01`); raising the voice (`ر ف ع:B010/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:93 `اسْمَعُوا`, `سَمِعْنَا`, `رَفَعْنَا`; 2:97, 2:102 `إِذْن`; 2:102 `تَتْلُوا`.
- Synthesis: Vocal production, sequential response, ear, and assent form a relay rather than an isolated act of hearing.

#### Subchannel B. Traces becoming recognition
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A follower tracks an earlier trace, identifies it by marks, and receives news from one who knows the group's condition.
- Active motifs: following an observable trace (`ق ف و:B001/m01`); tracking an أثر (`ق و ف:B001/m01`); recognition through a sign or trace (`ع ر ف:B003/m01`); group informant who knows its condition (`ع ر ف:B006/m01`); incoming transmitted report (`ن ب ء:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:87 `قَفَّيْنَا`; 2:89 `عَرَفُوا`; 2:91 `أَنْبِيَاء`; 2:93 `اسْمَعُوا`.
- Synthesis: Sequence becomes evidence: a predecessor leaves a track, the track enables recognition, and recognized knowledge is converted into report.

### 12. P6 (2:87-103) - Life-force entering and leaving the body
- Semantic invariant: An interior body is animated, constricted, relieved, filled, or emptied by what passes through it.
- Surface relation: indirect; 2:87, 2:93-96, and 2:102 anchor the channel in spirit, selves, life, death, hearts, and the image of being made to drink.
- Surprising reach: Comprehension and attachment take the form of drinking, so an inward conviction can be tasted, absorbed, or resisted like liquid.

#### Subchannel A. Breath, animation, and extinction
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Spirit and breath animate a body; breathing relieves constriction; their withdrawal leaves bodily or cardiac death.
- Active motifs: spirit that gives the body life (`ر و ح:B001/m01`); breath emerging from within (`ن ف س:B001/m01`); relief by opening a constriction (`ن ف س:B002/m01`); animate creature possessing spirit (`ح ي ي:B003/m01`); loss of force and life (`م و ت:B001/m01`); death-like failure of the heart (`م و ت:B006/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:87 `رُوح`; 2:87, 2:90, 2:102 `أَنفُس`; 2:94 `مَوْت`; 2:96 `حَيَاة`.
- Synthesis: Animation is modeled as an interior circulation. Breath and spirit sustain the living body, relief reopens it, and cessation empties life from body or heart.

#### Subchannel B. Understanding imbibed into the heart
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Meaning is drunk into an interior, where it may be sweet, resisted by the body, or diluted to reduce its force.
- Active motifs: drinking as understanding (`ش ر ب:B011/m01`); pleasant sweetness in drink or food (`ع ذ ب:B001/m01`); bodily refusal of intake (`ع ذ ب:B002/m01`); breaking a drink's severity with water (`ق ت ل:B007/m01`); heart as receiving interior (`ق ل ب:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:90, 2:96 `عَذَاب`; 2:87, 2:91 `تَقْتُلُون`; 2:93 `أُشْرِبُوا`, `قُلُوبِهِم`.
- Synthesis: The surface image of being made to drink into the heart opens a lexical physiology of belief: meaning becomes an ingestible substance with taste, force, and bodily uptake.

### 13. P7 (2:104-121) - Presented speech and evidence
- Semantic invariant: A claim is brought before another party in a form that can be delivered, spoken, tested, and either verified or exposed.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:104, 2:111, and 2:118 feature commanded speech, requested proof, truth claims, and demands for direct address.
- Surprising reach: A communicative mark can be either a meaningful word or a bodily wound, making evidence something said or visibly inscribed.

#### Subchannel A. Gift, demand, and proof
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: One party brings or gives an object, another demands its presentation, and the offered item functions as proof.
- Active motifs: giving and delivery (`ء ت ي:B002/m01`); demand to bring or present (`ه ا ت:B001/m01`); courteous dispatch of a gift (`ه د ي:B004/m01`); establishing a claim through proof (`ب ر ه ن:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:106, 2:109-110, 2:118, 2:121 forms of `أتى`; 2:111 `هَاتُوا`, `بُرْهَانَكُم`; 2:120 `هُدَى`.
- Synthesis: Delivery and demand converge in an evidentiary scene: what is brought must not merely be present but must establish the claim attached to it.

#### Subchannel B. Word as intelligible or injurious mark
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: An utterance connects speakers and defines a matter, while a cognate mark can be cut into a body as a wound.
- Active motifs: intelligible speech linking interlocutors (`ك ل م:B001/m01`); meaningful word or expression (`ك ل م:B002/m01`); bodily wound (`ك ل م:B003/m01`); utterance that defines a thing (`ق و ل:B016/m01`); truthfulness of speech (`ص د ق:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:104, 2:111, 2:113, 2:116-118, 2:120 forms of `قَوْل`; 2:118 `يُكَلِّمُنَا`; 2:111 `صَادِقِين`.
- Synthesis: Spoken meaning and visible wound share the function of leaving a legible mark. Truth determines whether the verbal mark accurately fixes what it names.

### 14. P7 (2:104-121) - Routes under guidance and authority
- Semantic invariant: A route becomes actionable when it is marked, led, claimed, and governed by one qualified to direct others.
- Surface relation: indirect; 2:107, 2:110, 2:114, and 2:120 anchor the channel in rule, striving, guidance, following, and affiliation.
- Surprising reach: Legal entitlement appears as pursuit along a path, while office and qualification determine who may direct that pursuit.

#### Subchannel A. Marked routes and pursuit
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Repeated traffic marks a road, branches create choices or traps, a leader takes the front, and a claimant follows.
- Active motifs: well-trodden marked road (`م ل ل:B006/m01`); worked or traveled road (`ع م ل:B011/m01`); branching or snaring path (`ش ر ك:B005/m01`); guide advancing at the front (`ه د ي:B003/m01`); claimant pursuing a right (`ت ب ع:B005/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:105 `مُشْرِكِين`; 2:110 `تَعْمَلُوا`; 2:120 `مِلَّتَهُم`, `هُدَى`, `تَتَّبِع`.
- Synthesis: Surface, branch, leader, and pursuer define a route system in which orientation is inseparable from the right being followed.

#### Subchannel B. Qualified governance
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A ruler or officeholder assumes responsibility because the office, priority, and competence properly belong to that person.
- Active motifs: assuming and administering an affair (`و ل ي:B003/m01`); priority and entitlement (`و ل ي:B008/m01`); governing office over a group (`س ع ي:B003/m01`); fitness and qualification (`ء ه ل:B003/m01`); sovereignty and authority (`م ل ك:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:105, 2:109 `أَهْل`; 2:107 `مُلْك`, `وَلِيّ`; 2:114 `سَعَى`; 2:115, 2:120 forms of `وَلِي`.
- Synthesis: Authority is resolved into title, entitlement, active administration, and fitness. The scene therefore concerns legitimate direction, not power in the abstract.

### 15. P8 (2:122-141) - Lineage as transmitted obligation
- Semantic invariant: Descent links a household across generations and carries entrusted obligations forward through that line.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:122-140 repeatedly names children, fathers, household, descendants, covenant, testament, and inherited affiliation.
- Surprising reach: A lineage is both biological branching and a custody chain through which an entrusted word reaches later members.

#### Subchannel A. Household and descent
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Parents generate a descending line whose children, household members, and tribal branches share an origin.
- Active motifs: fatherhood and nurture (`ء ب و:B001/m01`); sonship and descent from an origin (`ب ن ي:B007/m01`); group joined by nearness and belonging (`ء ه ل:B001/m01`); household and dependents (`ب ي ت:B002/m01`); genealogical branch and group (`س ب ط:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:122 `بَنِي`; 2:125, 2:127 `بَيْت`; 2:126 `أَهْل`; 2:133 `آبَائِك`, `بَنِيَّ`; 2:136, 2:140 `أَسْبَاط`.
- Synthesis: Parent, descendants, household, and sub-lineage make a nested social body in which belonging is organized by origin and branch.

#### Subchannel B. Covenant carried as legacy
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An earlier charge is deposited for safekeeping, conveyed to successors, and assigned to those it reaches.
- Active motifs: prior instruction entrusted for preservation (`ع ه د:B002/m01`); charge conveyed onward (`و ص ي:B002/m01`); reciprocal transmission of testament (`و ص ي:B003/m01`); assigning an entrusted good or harm (`و ل ي:B013/m01`); causing something to reach another (`ن ي ل:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:124-125 `عَهْد`; 2:124 `يَنَال`; 2:132 `وَصَّى`; 2:137 `تَوَلَّوْا`.
- Synthesis: The legacy scene has a temporal direction: an entrusted obligation originates earlier, is kept intact, and reaches a later bearer.

### 16. P8 (2:122-141) - Sacred formation of a community
- Semantic invariant: A community is formed by cleansing conduct and by transmitting signs, words, and discriminating knowledge.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:125, 2:128-131, and 2:136-140 connect purification, ritual posture, submission, recited signs, teaching, and wisdom.
- Surprising reach: Purity is both removal of stain and repair of social estrangement, while a sign can operate as word, example, or visible beacon.

#### Subchannel A. Purification through posture and peace
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Impurity and estrangement are removed as participants lower themselves, reconcile, and enter a state of peaceful submission.
- Active motifs: purity and moral soundness (`ز ك و:B002/m01`); removal of stain (`ط ه ر:B001/m01`); reconciliation opposed to war (`س ل م:B004/m01`); repair of social estrangement (`ص ل ح:B002/m01`); bodily lowering (`س ج د:B001/m01`); humility and self-lowering (`ر ك ع:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:125 `طَهِّر`, `الرُّكَّع`, `السُّجُود`; 2:128, 2:131-133, 2:136 forms of `سَلَم`; 2:129 `يُزَكِّيهِم`; 2:130 `الصَّالِحِين`.
- Synthesis: Cleansing is enacted at bodily and social levels: lowered posture removes self-assertion, while reconciliation removes communal friction.

#### Subchannel B. Signs made intelligible
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A visible sign is expressed in words and examples, raised like a beacon, and interpreted through knowledge and sound judgment.
- Active motifs: evident sign (`ء ي ي:B003/m01`); meaningful word (`ك ل م:B002/m01`); example functioning as lesson and sign (`م ث ل:B011/m01`); visible beacon (`ن و ر:B005/m01`); knowledge disclosed to a knower (`ع ل م:B001/m01`); accurate wisdom (`ح ك م:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:124 `كَلِمَات`; 2:126 `نَار`; 2:129 `آيَات`, `يُعَلِّم`, `حِكْمَة`; 2:137 `مِثْل`.
- Synthesis: Sign, word, analogy, and beacon are different carriers of legibility. Teaching and wisdom complete the scene by converting those carriers into understood guidance.

### 17. P9 (2:142-152) - Orientation by a governing axis
- Semantic invariant: Bodies and communities orient themselves by selecting a facing, locating a center, and regulating turns around that axis.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:142-150 repeatedly names east, west, middle, qibla, face, direction, turning, and reversal.
- Surprising reach: Orientation includes the body's heels and the act of flipping an object from its face, so communal redirection is also a concrete mechanics of turning.

#### Subchannel A. Face aligned to a direction
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A face confronts a selected direction and is deliberately turned toward a designated point.
- Active motifs: face and forward aspect (`و ج ه:B001/m01`); direction or orientation (`و ج ه:B002/m01`); one thing facing another (`ق ب ل:B001/m01`); prayer direction (`ق ب ل:B005/m01`); intended direction (`ش ط ر:B006/m01`); turning the face toward something (`و ل ي:B006/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:142-145 `قِبْلَة`; 2:144, 2:148-150 `وَجْه`, `وِجْهَة`; 2:144, 2:149-150 `شَطْر`; 2:142, 2:144, 2:148-150 forms of `وَلَّى`.
- Synthesis: Face, facing, destination, and intentional turning compose a precise orientation operation centered on a selected qibla.

#### Subchannel B. Center, horizons, and reversal
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: East and west establish opposing horizons, a middle mediates them, and a turn can reverse a subject onto its heels.
- Active motifs: sunrise from the east (`ش ر ق:B001/m01`); sunset and western horizon (`غ ر ب:B006/m01`); just or choice position in the middle (`و س ط:B001/m01`); center between extremes (`و س ط:B002/m01`); heel and rear footprint (`ع ق ب:B002/m01`); turning back on the heel (`ع ق ب:B003/m01`); flipping something away from its face (`ق ل ب:B004/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:142 `مَشْرِق`, `مَغْرِب`; 2:143 `وَسَطًا`, `عَقِبَيْه`, `يَنقَلِب`; 2:144 `تَقَلُّب`.
- Synthesis: The channel supplies a full axis and a bodily reversal mechanism. Center and horizons define the field; heel and overturned face describe motion within it.

### 18. P9 (2:142-152) - Public transmission of known truth
- Semantic invariant: Knowledge becomes communal when a recognized truth is witnessed, recited, taught, and not concealed.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:143, 2:146, and 2:151 connect witness, recognition, concealment, messenger, recitation, purification, book, teaching, and wisdom.
- Surprising reach: Recitation is structurally a following act, so transmission preserves both semantic content and temporal succession.

#### Subchannel A. Recognition, testimony, and concealment
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A knower recognizes a true matter, attends as witness, states it from knowledge, or suppresses it.
- Active motifs: presence with direct observation (`ش ه د:B001/m01`); declaration grounded in knowledge (`ش ه د:B002/m01`); recognition through a mark (`ع ر ف:B003/m01`); hiding and withholding (`ك ت م:B001/m01`); fixed and binding truth (`ح ق ق:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:143 `شُهَدَاء`, `شَهِيدًا`; 2:144, 2:146-147, 2:149 `حَق`; 2:146 `يَعْرِفُون`, `يَكْتُمُون`.
- Synthesis: Recognition supplies the epistemic basis, testimony makes it public, and concealment reverses that movement by retaining what should be declared.

#### Subchannel B. Recitation, cleansing, and instruction
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A commissioned messenger recites a transmitted text, purifies recipients, and teaches discriminating knowledge.
- Active motifs: sending and commissioning (`ر س ل:B001/m01`); messenger bearing a message (`ر س ل:B002/m01`); following in sequence (`ت ل و:B001/m01`); purification and soundness (`ز ك و:B002/m01`); knowledge disclosed to the learner (`ع ل م:B001/m01`); composed written text (`ك ت ب:B002/m01`); accurate wisdom (`ح ك م:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:143, 2:151 `رَسُول`; 2:151 `أَرْسَلْنَا`, `يَتْلُوا`, `يُزَكِّيكُم`, `يُعَلِّمُكُم`, `كِتَاب`, `حِكْمَة`.
- Synthesis: Commission, serial recitation, moral formation, and instruction create an ordered pedagogy in which a text is carried into communal understanding.

### 19. P10 (2:153-177) - Water moving from atmosphere to land
- Semantic invariant: Moisture gathers above, descends through the air, collects below, and enables life.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:164 names sky, cloud, descending water, revival of earth, and atmospheric ordering.
- Surprising reach: Cloud morphology ranges from drawn-out and encircling to white-stacked and dark, while fallen water can become puddle or river.

#### Subchannel A. Formed cloud mass
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Moisture gathers into a cloud body whose shape may be trailing, piled, darkened, or ringed.
- Active motifs: rain-bearing cloud (`ر ب ب:B008/m01`); drawn-out cloud (`س ح ب:B002/m01`); piled white cloud (`ص ب ر:B010/m01`); dark cloud mass (`ع م ي:B005/m01`); encircling crown (`ك ل ل:B005/m01`); overhanging sky (`س م و:B004/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:164 `السَّمَاوَات`, `السَّمَاء`, `السَّحَاب`, `كُلِّ`; 2:153, 2:155, 2:175, 2:177 forms of `صَبَر`.
- Synthesis: The cloud is treated as a structured atmospheric body with volume, edge, density, and position under the sky.

#### Subchannel B. Descent, collection, and terrestrial life
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Returning water falls between cloud and ground, gathers in a low basin or channel, and revives living systems.
- Active motifs: rain as returning water (`ر ج ع:B006/m01`); rain streaming between cloud and earth (`س ب ل:B005/m01`); pool of collected water (`س ح ب:B007/m01`); earth made alive by rain (`ح ي ي:B002/m01`); river cutting the ground (`ن ه ر:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:154, 2:164 `أَحْيَاء`, `أَحْيَا`; 2:154, 2:177 `سَبِيل`; 2:156 `رَاجِعُون`; 2:164 `السَّحَاب`, `النَّهَار`.
- Synthesis: Falling, pooling, channeling, and revival give the atmospheric image a downstream terrestrial process.

### 20. P10 (2:153-177) - Provision incorporated by bodies and households
- Semantic invariant: Material provision is apportioned, consumed, and redistributed to sustain bodies and vulnerable members of a social body.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:168, 2:172, 2:174, and 2:177 join eating and provision with kin, orphans, the poor, travelers, and liberation.
- Surprising reach: The same nutritive logic that builds flesh also governs social distribution: a household can be fed as a collective body.

#### Subchannel A. Food becoming bodily growth
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An allotted gift becomes edible sustenance, builds flesh, and appears as increasing produce or wealth.
- Active motifs: edible share (`ء ك ل:B003/m01`); apportioned gift (`ر ز ق:B001/m01`); food that nourishes (`ر ز ق:B002/m01`); food building flesh (`ب ن ي:B010/m01`); growing produce or wealth (`ث م ر:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:155 `الثَّمَرَات`; 2:168, 2:172, 2:174 forms of `أَكَل`; 2:172 `رَزَقْنَاكُم`; 2:177 `ابْن`.
- Synthesis: Allocation and ingestion culminate in growth, making nourishment a material conversion rather than a static possession.

#### Subchannel B. Care distributed through the social body
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Family and community distribute resources to kin, children without guardians, the poor, and travelers.
- Active motifs: fatherhood and nurture (`ء ب و:B001/m01`); descent and child relation (`ب ن ي:B007/m01`); blood kinship (`ق ر ب:B003/m01`); child cut off from a guardian (`ي ت م:B001/m01`); traveler and road-user (`س ب ل:B002/m01`); condition of poverty and abasement (`س ك ن:B006/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:170 `آبَاء`; 2:177 `قُرْبَى`, `يَتَامَى`, `مَسَاكِين`, `ابْنَ السَّبِيل`.
- Synthesis: The recipients form a structured care network. Kinship supplies ordinary attachment, while orphan, poor person, and traveler mark points where support must cross missing or weakened ties.

### 21. P11 (2:178-203) - Time bounded by thresholds
- Semantic invariant: Human action is organized by recurring units and by limits that may be approached, reached, or crossed.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:184-203 supplies counted days, month, crescent phases, night, approach, completion, and repeated limits.
- Surprising reach: Recitation carries a latent cyclical sense of gathering at an appointed time, binding textual reading to calendar recurrence.

#### Subchannel A. Calendar recurrence
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A visible crescent initiates a month, days and nights compose its duration, and recurring time returns to an appointed phase.
- Active motifs: month known by its crescent (`ش ه ر:B001/m01`); first appearance of the crescent (`ه ل ل:B001/m01`); bounded daytime unit (`ي و م:B001/m01`); night adjacent to a day (`ل ي ل:B003/m01`); appointed time and cyclic return (`ق ر ء:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:184-185, 2:196, 2:203 `أَيَّام`, `يَوْمَيْن`; 2:185, 2:194, 2:197 `شَهْر`, `أَشْهُر`; 2:187 `لَيْلَة`; 2:189 `أَهِلَّة`; 2:185 `قُرْآن`.
- Synthesis: Celestial sign, month, day-night units, and recurring appointment create a calendar mechanism for timing obligations.

#### Subchannel B. Approaching and reaching a limit
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A subject nears a boundary, comes into contact with it, reaches the terminal point, and is required to stop there.
- Active motifs: nearness (`ق ر ب:B001/m01`); close contact or approach (`ق ر ب:B007/m01`); terminal point (`ء ل ي:B001/m01`); arrival at an endpoint (`ب ل غ:B001/m01`); limit at which a process stops (`ن ه ي:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:180, 2:186-187 `أَقْرَبِين`, `قَرِيب`, `تَقْرَبُوا`; 2:192-193 `انتَهَوْا`; 2:196 `يَبْلُغ`.
- Synthesis: Nearness, contact, arrival, and cessation are distinct stages of one boundary process, clarifying how a prescribed limit governs action before and at its endpoint.

### 22. P11 (2:178-203) - Transfer under protection
- Semantic invariant: A burden or entitlement can pass between parties only through a rule that preserves persons, kin, and outstanding claims.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:178-184 and 2:196 join required following, brotherhood, payment, testament, death, protection, and ransom.
- Surprising reach: Ransom and legal liability share a substitution mechanism: one burden stands in place of another to prevent direct harm.

#### Subchannel A. Liability, substitution, and ransom
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A liability adheres to a person, a substitute or guarantor takes its place, and payment averts the threatened consequence.
- Active motifs: attached liability (`ت ب ع:B006/m01`); substitute or guarantee (`ع ق ب:B010/m01`); warding something off by substitution (`ف د ي:B003/m01`); protection that repels harm (`و ق ي:B001/m01`); placing oneself within protection (`و ق ي:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:178 `اتِّبَاع`; 2:179-180, 2:183, 2:187, 2:189, 2:194, 2:196-197, 2:201, 2:203 forms of `وَقَى`; 2:184, 2:196 `فِدْيَة`; 2:196 `عِقَاب`.
- Synthesis: The channel organizes protection through transfer: liability is recognized, a substitute is supplied, and harm is intercepted.

#### Subchannel B. Testament securing kin after death
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A dying person transmits a binding charge that preserves the claims of siblings, blood relatives, and protected family members.
- Active motifs: charge conveyed onward (`و ص ي:B002/m01`); mutual testament (`و ص ي:B003/m01`); sibling bond (`ء خ و:B001/m01`); blood kinship (`ق ر ب:B003/m01`); protected close relatives and women (`ح ر م:B011/m01`); loss of life (`م و ت:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:178 `أَخِيه`; 2:180 `مَوْت`, `وَصِيَّة`, `أَقْرَبِين`; 2:182 `مُوص`; 2:191, 2:194, 2:196, 2:198 forms of `حَرَام`.
- Synthesis: Death initiates a controlled handoff. Testament carries obligation across that rupture so kinship claims remain operative after the original holder is gone.

### 23. P12 (2:204-220) - Labor and material consequence
- Semantic invariant: Intentional work changes a field or social environment toward maintenance, corruption, destruction, or repair.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:204-205, 2:212, 2:215, 2:217, and 2:220 foreground deeds, field destruction, corruption, reform, and continuing action.
- Surprising reach: The labor lexicon includes hands trained or imprinted by work, making repeated action a property of the worker as well as the product.

#### Subchannel A. Workers shaped by repeated action
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Agents deliberately act, labor with their hands, and become habituated or marked by continued work.
- Active motifs: intentional deed and labor (`ع م ل:B001/m01`); manual workforce (`ع م ل:B006/m01`); one imprinted or habituated by work (`ع م ل:B008/m01`); unit or instance of work (`ف ع ل:B003/m01`); continued action (`ز ي ل:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:215 `تَفْعَلُوا`; 2:217 `أَعْمَال`; 2:217 `يَزَالُون`.
- Synthesis: Act, worker, repeated unit, and habituation form a process in which continued labor shapes both material results and the agent's disposition.

#### Subchannel B. Field damaged or restored
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Work gathers and cultivates value, corruption disorders it, destruction removes it, and repair returns it to fitness.
- Active motifs: gathering, earning, and working a field (`ح ر ث:B001/m01`); departure from sound order (`ف س د:B001/m01`); destruction and loss (`ه ل ك:B001/m01`); restoration opposed to corruption (`ص ل ح:B001/m01`); benefit through watering and repair (`غ ي ر:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:205 `حَرْث`, `يُفْسِد`, `فَسَاد`, `يُهْلِك`; 2:212 `غَيْر`; 2:220 `إِصْلَاح`, `مُصْلِح`, `مُفْسِد`.
- Synthesis: The scene tracks a worked substrate through opposed outcomes. Corruption and destruction degrade accumulated value; repair and beneficial tending restore its capacity.

### 24. P12 (2:204-220) - Routes under obstruction and aid
- Semantic invariant: Movement toward a destination depends on whether a path is opened, supplied, blocked, or diverted.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:208, 2:213, 2:215, and 2:217-218 name a straight path, way, obstruction from the way, and adversarial diversion.
- Surprising reach: Rain and irrigation can serve as route-making aid, so guidance is supported by a material infrastructure of water and relief.

#### Subchannel A. Rain-supported passage
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Travelers move along a road while rain, irrigation, and timely relief sustain the land and those crossing it.
- Active motifs: road-users and travelers (`س ب ل:B002/m01`); rain as relief (`ن ص ر:B004/m01`); rain following the first seasonal shower (`و ل ي:B010/m01`); descending rain as provision (`ر ز ق:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:205 `تَوَلَّى`; 2:212 `يَرْزُق`; 2:214 `نَصْر`; 2:215, 2:217-218 `سَبِيل`.
- Synthesis: Route and rainfall form a support scene: passage is possible because relief reaches both terrain and traveler.

#### Subchannel B. Branching, blockage, and diversion
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A straight route is surrounded by lesser tracks, a passage toward water can be blocked, and a distant adversary diverts travelers from their course.
- Active motifs: small branching tracks (`ب ن ي:B008/m01`); road leading toward water (`ص د د:B004/m01`); straight road (`ص ر ط:B001/m01`); distant and severing adversary (`ش ط ن:B001/m01`); deflection from the right course (`ف ت ن:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:208 `الشَّيْطَان`; 2:211, 2:215 forms of `بَنِي`; 2:213 `صِرَاط`; 2:217 `صَدّ`, `فِتْنَة`.
- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes route structure from route failure: subsidiary tracks complicate choice, obstruction blocks access, and diversion moves the traveler onto the wrong course.

### 25. P13 (2:221-242) - Binding and releasing a union
- Semantic invariant: A social union is created by binding parties under an agreement and ended by operations that loosen, sever, retain, or release that bond.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:221, 2:227-237, and 2:240-241 densely repeat marriage, knot, divorce, retention, release, and obstruction.
- Surprising reach: Marriage law is rendered as knot mechanics: the bond can be tightened, untied, cut beyond return, held, or allowed to move free.

#### Subchannel A. Contracting a marital bond
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Two people are paired, a binding agreement is concluded, and the union becomes operative for themselves or through another arranger.
- Active motifs: marital spouse (`ز و ج:B002/m01`); pairing one thing with another (`ز و ج:B003/m01`); binding and ratifying a covenant (`ع ق د:B002/m01`); concluding one's marriage contract (`ن ك ح:B002/m01`); arranging marriage for another (`ن ك ح:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:221, 2:230, 2:232, 2:235, 2:237 forms of `نِكَاح`; 2:230, 2:232, 2:234, 2:240 `زَوْج`, `أَزْوَاج`; 2:235, 2:237 `عُقْدَة`.
- Synthesis: Pairing supplies the relation, while the contract fixes it as an obligation. The distinction between self-contract and arranging another's marriage preserves the scene's separate social roles.

#### Subchannel B. Unbinding, retention, and release
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A marital bond is untied or severed, after which one party may retain the other rightly, obstruct departure, or release without hindrance.
- Active motifs: untying a knot (`ح ل ل:B001/m01`); freeing the marriage tether (`ط ل ق:B002/m01`); divorce cutting off return (`ب ي ن:B012/m01`); constricting obstruction of a right (`ع ض ل:B004/m01`); holding and retaining (`م س ك:B001/m01`); unhindered release (`س ر ح:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:228-230 `يَحِلّ`, `طَلَاق`, `طَلَّق`; 2:229, 2:231 `إِمْسَاك`, `أَمْسِكُوا`, `تُمْسِكُوا`, `تَسْرِيح`, `سَرِّحُوهُن`; 2:232 `تَعْضُلُوا`; 2:232, 2:237 `بَيْن`.
- Synthesis: Dissolution is not a single event but a controlled sequence of untying, possible retention, prohibited obstruction, and free release.

### 26. P13 (2:221-242) - Dependent life from gestation to separation
- Semantic invariant: New life begins enclosed and dependent, is nourished through another body, and gradually separates into independent existence.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:222-223, 2:228, and 2:233 join reproductive cycles, wombs, parents, children, nursing, and weaning.
- Surprising reach: The dependent-young pattern extends from infant care to a horticultural nursery of young palms without merging plant and human scenes.

#### Subchannel A. Womb, cycle, and birth
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A reproductive cycle prepares the womb, hidden life gathers there, birth opens the body, and postpartum blood or pain follows.
- Active motifs: fetus hidden in the abdomen (`ج ن ن:B007/m01`); female womb (`ر ح م:B003/m01`); postpartum uterine pain (`ر ح م:B004/m01`); menstrual flow (`ح ي ض:B001/m01`); childbirth and postpartum bleeding (`ن ف س:B005/m01`); womb gathering and carrying (`ق ر ء:B003/m01`); occurrence of birth (`و ل د:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:221 `جَنَّة`; 2:222 `مَحِيض`; 2:228 `أَرْحَام`, `قُرُوء`, `أَنفُس`; 2:233 `وَالِدَات`, `مَوْلُود`, `وَلَد`.
- Synthesis: Cyclical preparation, enclosure, gestation, delivery, and postpartum aftermath form one reproductive process with distinct bodily stages.

#### Subchannel B. Nursing and weaning
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A newborn receives milk from a caregiver, remains attached during infancy, and is then separated from breast and mother.
- Active motifs: suckling and provision of breast milk (`ر ض ع:B001/m01`); infant separated from mother or nursing (`ف ص ل:B003/m01`); young animal sent alongside its mother (`ر ج ل:B014/m01`); offspring produced by descent (`و ل د:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:228, 2:239 `رِجَال`; 2:233 `يُرْضِعْن`, `رَضَاعَة`, `تَسْتَرْضِعُوا`, `فِصَالًا`, `وَالِدَات`, `أَوْلَاد`.
- Synthesis: The subchannel follows dependence through feeding and accompanying the mother to the threshold at which the young is separated.

#### Subchannel C. Horticultural nursery
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Young palms stand as dependent growths that require cultivation before they become mature trees.
- Active motifs: small palm shoots named through suckling (`ر ض ع:B005/m01`); short or young palms (`ج ع ل:B006/m01`); young palm trees (`ش ي ء:B006/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:224 `تَجْعَلُوا`; 2:223, 2:229, 2:231 `شِئْتُم`, `شَيْئًا`; 2:233 forms of `رَضَع`.
- Synthesis: The lexical nursery preserves the parent invariant at a different scale: immature life remains dependent on a sustaining environment before separation and full growth.

### 27. P13 (2:221-242) - Measured delay and capacity
- Semantic invariant: An obligation is governed both by when its term is reached and by how much burden a person can bear.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:226, 2:231-236, and 2:242 repeatedly mark waiting, appointed terms, reaching limits, capacity, measure, and imposed burden.
- Surprising reach: Temporal restraint and physical capacity are parallel controls: one delays action until the right point, the other limits action to a bearable amount.

#### Subchannel A. Delay until an appointed term
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Action is slowed or held back through an interval, proceeds toward an appointed endpoint, and changes when that endpoint is reached.
- Active motifs: deliberate delay (`ء ن ي:B001/m01`); slowing and holding back (`ء ل ي:B013/m01`); fixed term (`ء ج ل:B001/m01`); arrival at an endpoint (`ب ل غ:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:223 `أَنَّى`; 2:226 `يُؤْلُون`; 2:231-232, 2:234-235 `أَجَل`, `بَلَغْن`, `يَبْلُغْن`.
- Synthesis: Waiting is structured by a destination in time. Delay holds the subject within the interval; reaching the term changes the available action.

#### Subchannel B. Burden calibrated to ability
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A duty or expense is measured against the actor's effective power, room, and tolerance for hardship.
- Active motifs: attainment of ability (`ء ل و:B002/m01`); effective power to act (`ق د ر:B003/m01`); breadth of capacity and endurance (`و س ع:B002/m01`); imposed hardship or right (`ك ل ف:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:226 `يُؤْلُون`; 2:233 `وُسْع`, `تُكَلَّف`; 2:236 `قَدَرُه`, `مُوسِع`.
- Synthesis: Ability is treated as measurable room. Obligation remains proportionate when its size does not exceed that room.

### 28. P14 (2:243-253) - Mobilized contest
- Semantic invariant: A group enters open confrontation by emerging, assembling force, enduring restraint, and receiving support.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:243-253 repeatedly names departure, battle, troops, endurance, killing, victory, and divine strengthening.
- Surprising reach: Readiness for battle begins with exposure in open ground, while supporting “hands” distribute force across power and aid.

#### Subchannel A. Emergence into open confrontation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Hidden or enclosed participants move outward into open space, form opposing sides, and enter mutual combat.
- Active motifs: becoming visible (`ب ر ز:B001/m01`); open exposed ground (`ب ر ز:B002/m01`); passing to the outside (`خ ر ج:B001/m01`); bringing something out of concealment (`خ ر ج:B002/m01`); fighting between two sides (`ق ت ل:B011/m01`); mutual resistance in battle (`ق و م:B014/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:243 `خَرَجُوا`; 2:244, 2:246, 2:251, 2:253 forms of `قَاتَل`, `قَتَل`, `اقْتَتَل`; 2:246 `أُخْرِجْنَا`; 2:250 `بَرَزُوا`, `قَوْم`.
- Synthesis: Exit and exposure are preparatory stages of contest. Once parties occupy the open field, resistance becomes reciprocal combat.

#### Subchannel B. Force, endurance, and aid
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Strength is supplied to combatants, maintained under coercive pressure, and converted into protection or victory.
- Active motifs: strengthening force (`ء ي د:B001/m01`); hand as power (`ي د ي:B002/m01`); supporting hand (`ي د ي:B016/m01`); restraint under killing or coercion (`ص ب ر:B002/m01`); taking life (`ق ت ل:B001/m01`); exposure to being killed (`ق ت ل:B005/m01`); aid that makes one side prevail (`ن ص ر:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:244, 2:246, 2:251, 2:253 forms of `قَتَل`; 2:249 `يَد`; 2:249-250 `صَابِرِين`, `صَبْرًا`, `انصُرْنَا`; 2:253 `أَيَّدْنَا`.
- Synthesis: Power is supplied through strengthening and aid, embodied as a hand, and tested by the capacity to remain under lethal pressure.

### 29. P14 (2:243-253) - Authority carried by message and judgment
- Semantic invariant: Leadership becomes legitimate and effective through elevated commission, knowledgeable rule, careful deliberation, and responsive hearing.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:246-253 connects prophet, king, kingdom, wisdom, truth, messengers, speech, and hearing.
- Surprising reach: Sovereignty has a route dimension: a ruler possesses and directs a path, while prophetic elevation supplies a vantage from which that path can be guided.

#### Subchannel A. Prophetic and royal direction
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An elevated bearer of news exercises learned authority over a people and controls the route along which they move.
- Active motifs: bearer of divine news (`ن ب ء:B003/m01`); elevation and high position (`ن ب و:B001/m01`); guiding road (`ن ب و:B005/m01`); sovereignty (`م ل ك:B003/m01`); controller of road or valley (`م ل ك:B006/m01`); sound judgment and wisdom (`ح ك م:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:246-248 `نَبِيّ`; 2:246-248, 2:251 `مَلِك`, `مُلْك`; 2:251 `حِكْمَة`; 2:252-253 `مُرْسَلِين`, `رُسُل`.
- Synthesis: Elevation, message, dominion, route control, and wisdom form a leadership scene in which authority both knows the course and directs collective movement.

#### Subchannel B. Deliberation before commission
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A matter is examined, established as true, discussed carefully, communicated without haste, and received with understanding.
- Active motifs: careful examination (`ث ب ت:B005/m01`); establishing and displaying truth (`ح ق ق:B005/m01`); deliberateness in speech and action (`ر س ل:B004/m01`); mutual discussion of a matter (`ق و ل:B009/m01`); hearing as understanding and compliance (`س م ع:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:244 `سَمِيع`; 2:246-250 forms of `قَال`; 2:250 `ثَبِّت`; 2:252 `حَق`, `مُرْسَلِين`.
- Synthesis: Leadership is preceded by an epistemic procedure: inspect, establish, deliberate, communicate, and secure informed compliance.

### 30. P15 (2:254-266) - Substrate that yields or nullifies return
- Semantic invariant: What falls on a substrate produces growth only when the receiving surface can hold, nourish, and return value.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:264-266 contrast exposed soil, downpour, dew, productive garden, palms, and destructive fire.
- Surprising reach: Failed generosity is imaged through several null returns: an idle surface, an unavenged claim, and a hand hardened against giving.

#### Subchannel A. Cultivated palm garden
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Young palms gather into a planted stand, vegetation thickens, and flowering marks successful growth.
- Active motifs: young or short palms (`ج ع ل:B006/m01`); young palm trees (`ش ي ء:B006/m01`); gathered stand of palms (`ص و ر:B005/m01`); palm tree (`ن خ ل:B001/m01`); dense surging vegetation (`ج ن ن:B011/m01`); blossom of a tree (`ن و ر:B004/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:259-260 `نَجْعَل`, `اجْعَل`; 2:259, 2:261, 2:264 `شَيْء`; 2:260 `صُرْ`; 2:265-266 `جَنَّة`; 2:266 `نَخِيل`, `نَار`.
- Synthesis: Shoot, tree, stand, dense growth, and flower describe a garden developing from dependent plants into a productive canopy.

#### Subchannel B. Rain on an exposed surface
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Heavy rain or dew strikes bare soil, whose posture and texture determine whether moisture remains or runs away.
- Active motifs: light moistening rain (`ط ل ل:B001/m01`); earth and loose soil (`ت ر ب:B001/m01`); heavy downpour (`و ب ل:B001/m01`); lying low against the ground (`م ث ل:B006/m01`); hand hardened and unyielding (`ص ل د:B004/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:261, 2:264-265 `مَثَل`; 2:264 `تُرَاب`, `صَلْدًا`, `وَابِل`; 2:265 `وَابِل`, `طَلّ`.
- Synthesis: Precipitation alone does not determine yield. The receiving surface may be low and receptive or hard and unable to retain what strikes it.

#### Subchannel C. Benefit rendered void
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Expected value is disabled, a claim is allowed to lapse, and the giver's hand withholds productive return.
- Active motifs: cessation of useful work (`ب ط ل:B005/m01`); blood claim left without compensation (`ب ط ل:B006/m01`); right or blood rendered void (`ط ل ل:B005/m01`); ungiving hardened hand (`ص ل د:B004/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:264 `تُبْطِلُوا`, `صَلْدًا`; 2:265 `طَلّ`.
- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes material barrenness from juridical and social nullification, but all three share the same outcome: a potential return is made nonoperative.

### 31. P15 (2:254-266) - Cognition through reanimation
- Semantic invariant: Understanding occurs when perception turns inward, stillness is interrupted, and apparently dead matter is recognized as capable of renewed life.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:258-260 and 2:266 repeatedly command seeing and reflection while staging death, revival, stillness, and reassurance of the heart.
- Surprising reach: Sleep, trustful stillness, death, and vegetative revival occupy a graded continuum rather than isolated categories.

#### Subchannel A. The heart seeing and thinking
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Eye and inward faculty attend to an event, turn it over, and arrive at reflective understanding.
- Active motifs: insight of the heart (`ب ص ر:B002/m01`); heart as inward organ (`ق ل ب:B001/m01`); inward opinion and reflection (`ر ء ي:B002/m01`); repeated turning of a matter in the heart (`ف ك ر:B001/m01`); directing sight or insight toward an object (`ن ظ ر:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:258, 2:260, 2:264 `تَرَ`, `أَرِنِي`, `رِئَاء`; 2:259 `انظُر`; 2:260 `قَلْبِي`; 2:265 `بَصِير`; 2:266 `تَتَفَكَّرُون`.
- Synthesis: Observation becomes cognition through an inward loop: direct attention, heart-level seeing, sustained consideration, and reflective judgment.

#### Subchannel B. Stillness, death, and return to life
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A body or landscape enters sleep-like stillness, settles after disturbance, and then returns from death into animation or growth.
- Active motifs: sleep-like stillness or decay (`م و ت:B012/m01`); settling into trust (`ن و م:B005/m01`); sleep as death (`ن و م:B008/m01`); calm after agitation (`ط م ن:B001/m01`); tranquility (`ط م ء ن:B001/m01`); earth revived through rain and plants (`ح ي ي:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:255 `نَوْم`; 2:258-260 forms of `مَات`, `يُحْيِي`, `مَوْتَى`; 2:260 `يَطْمَئِن`; 2:266 `نَار`.
- Synthesis: Sleep and calm model reversible stillness, death marks its extreme, and revival demonstrates that apparent cessation can be reopened into life.

### 32. P16 (2:267-286) - Growth through financial transfer
- Semantic invariant: Wealth moves out from one holder and either nourishes increase or becomes an imposed, harmful extraction.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:267-278 contrasts spending, provision, charity, alms, usury, increase, and the consequences of financial conduct.
- Surprising reach: Monetary increase is compared with biological nurture, while levies and wages expose the institutional machinery behind transfer.

#### Subchannel A. Nurtured increase
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Provision is released through spending and then cultivated into growth rather than accumulated through usury.
- Active motifs: tending something to completion (`ر ب ب:B002/m01`); feeding and developmental growth (`ر ب و:B005/m01`); increase and flourishing (`ز ك و:B001/m01`); money going out as expenditure (`ن ف ق:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:267, 2:270, 2:272-274 forms of `أَنفَق`; 2:274 `رَب`; 2:275-276, 2:278 `رِبَا`, `يُرْبِي`; 2:277 `الزَّكَاة`.
- Synthesis: Financial circulation is rendered as cultivation: provision leaves the giver, enters a field of care, and returns as legitimate growth.

#### Subchannel B. Levies, wages, and injurious extraction
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Authorities assess payments, workers receive compensation, and coercive transfer can injure or become a basis for boasting over the recipient.
- Active motifs: assessed levy (`ء ت ي:B008/m01`); imposed payment (`ض ر ب:B010/m01`); wage or worker's provision (`ع م ل:B004/m01`); manual labor force (`ع م ل:B006/m01`); causing reciprocal harm (`ض ر ر:B002/m01`); wealth gathered into a lump (`ض ر ر:B006/m01`); claiming praise through a favor (`ح م د:B005/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:267 `أَنفِقُوا`, `حَمِيد`; 2:269, 2:271, 2:277 forms of `آتَى`; 2:271, 2:277, 2:283 `تَعْمَلُون`, `عَمِلُوا`; 2:273 `ضَرْبًا`; 2:282 `يُضَارّ`.
- Synthesis: Transfer has institutional roles: assessor, payer, worker, and recipient. The channel also marks failure modes in which payment becomes coercive, harmful, or self-glorifying.

### 33. P16 (2:267-286) - Recorded obligation and guarantee
- Semantic invariant: A claim becomes durable when responsibility is assigned, the terms are fixed in writing, and persons or property secure performance.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:282-283 densely joins debt, term, writing, witnesses, performance, pledge, possession, and concealment of testimony.
- Surprising reach: Moral liability and commercial surety share a carrying mechanism: a person, document, or pledged object bears the claim until it is discharged.

#### Subchannel A. Surety carrying an obligation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A person accepts responsibility for a binding claim, carries it as guarantor, and preserves its reality until settlement.
- Active motifs: assuming a guarantee (`ق ب ل:B008/m01`); standing surety for another (`ك و ن:B003/m01`); financial or blood-money guarantee (`ح م ل:B004/m01`); binding entitlement (`ح ق ق:B002/m01`); reality that must be preserved (`ح ق ق:B007/m01`); covering and removing liability (`ك ف ر:B009/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:271, 2:276, 2:286 forms of `كَفَر`; 2:278, 2:280, 2:282-283 forms of `كَان`; 2:282 `حَق`; 2:286 `قَبْل`, `تَحْمِل`, `حَمَلْنَا`, `تُحَمِّلْ`.
- Synthesis: Guarantee relocates but does not erase the claim. A responsible party carries it, preserves its binding reality, and seeks final covering only through discharge.

#### Subchannel B. Written, witnessed, and pledged transfer
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A debt is fixed in a document, witnessed by knowledgeable participants, performed as a right, and secured by property placed in hand.
- Active motifs: composed written record (`ك ت ب:B002/m01`); written fixing that imposes judgment (`ك ت ب:B003/m01`); presence as witness (`ش ه د:B001/m01`); declaration from knowledge (`ش ه د:B002/m01`); performance of a right or trust (`ء د ي:B002/m01`); pledged object held for a right (`ر ه ن:B001/m01`); taking by a closed hand (`ق ب ض:B001/m01`); possession and collection of property (`ق ب ض:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:282-283 forms of `كَتَب`, `شَهِد`; 2:283 `يُؤَدِّ`, `رِهَان`, `مَقْبُوضَة`.
- Synthesis: Writing fixes terms, witnesses make them publicly knowable, performance satisfies them, and a pledge gives the creditor a material security.

### 34. P16 (2:267-286) - Need answered by voluntary relief
- Semantic invariant: Material lack becomes socially reparable when need can be recognized without coercive asking and surplus is released as an unburdened gift.
- Surface relation: direct; 2:268, 2:271-273, and 2:280 contrast poverty, concealed need, importunate asking, wealth, hardship, giving, and voluntary good.
- Surprising reach: Relief includes not only the object given but the manner of giving: ease, generosity, and a willing disposition are part of the transfer.

#### Subchannel A. Poverty, request, and constrained need
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A person lacks resources, may request help insistently or remain outwardly self-sufficient, and can fall into financial constriction.
- Active motifs: request and solicitation (`س ء ل:B001/m01`); importunate asking (`ل ح ف:B003/m01`); material need and poverty (`ف ق ر:B002/m01`); constricted means (`ع س ر:B002/m01`); wealth and self-sufficiency (`غ ن ي:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:267 `غَنِيّ`; 2:268 `فَقْر`; 2:271, 2:273 `فُقَرَاء`; 2:273 `أَغْنِيَاء`, `يَسْأَلُون`, `إِلْحَافًا`; 2:280 `عُسْرَة`.
- Synthesis: Need is legible through a contrast between actual lack and outward restraint. Asking is one signal, but the absence of asking does not imply sufficiency.

#### Subchannel B. Easy surplus and generous release
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A giver identifies expendable surplus, seeks the good, and releases it freely as gift, relief, or generous support.
- Active motifs: easy surplus left available (`ع ف و:B003/m01`); seeking good and livelihood (`ع ف و:B004/m01`); benefaction and gift (`ف ض ل:B003/m01`); generosity and donation (`خ ي ر:B005/m01`); aid as an act of giving (`ن ص ر:B005/m01`); ease and willing generosity (`ر س ل:B010/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:268 `فَضْلًا`; 2:269, 2:271-273, 2:280 `خَيْر`; 2:279, 2:285 `رَسُول`, `رُسُل`; 2:286 `اعْفُ`, `انصُرْنَا`.
- Synthesis: Relief is a voluntary flow from available surplus toward recognized need. Its defining quality is ease rather than pressure on either giver or receiver.

## Standalone Subchannels

### S1. P1 (2:1-20) - Hidden palm growth
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Roots remain unseen below ground while a palm's core, young shoots, branches, and flowers develop above.
- Active motifs: hidden roots of a tree (`غ ي ب:B008/m01`); palm or tree core (`ق ل ب:B003/m01`); tree blossom (`ن و ر:B004/m01`); young palm trees (`ش ي ء:B006/m01`); tall spreading tree (`ظ ل م:B007/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:3 `غَيْب`; 2:7, 2:10 `قُلُوب`; 2:17 `نُور`; 2:17, 2:19-20 forms of `ظُلْم`; 2:20 `شَيْء`.
- Synthesis: Below-ground concealment, interior core, juvenile growth, spreading tree, and blossom form a complete developmental profile of a palm.

### S2. P1 (2:1-20) - Market circulation and collapse
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Merchandise enters a lively market, circulates while demand persists, then falls still and disappears from exchange.
- Active motifs: she-camel circulating as saleable merchandise (`ت ج ر:B003/m01`); briskness of a market (`ق و م:B018/m01`); stillness and decay (`م و ت:B012/m01`); exhaustion and disappearance (`ن ف ق:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:3 `يُنفِقُون`; 2:16 `تِجَارَتُهُم`; 2:19 `مَوْت`; 2:20 `قَامُوا`.
- Synthesis: Merchandise, market activity, stagnation, and exhaustion describe a commercial life cycle whose failed endpoint resonates with the explicit unprofitable trade.

### S3. P2 (2:21-39) - Sign, utterance, and beacon
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A sign becomes intelligible as a word or analogy and visible as an elevated marker.
- Active motifs: evident sign (`ء ي ي:B003/m01`); meaningful word (`ك ل م:B002/m01`); example functioning as lesson and sign (`م ث ل:B011/m01`); visible beacon (`ن و ر:B005/m01`); elevated or enclosed textual unit (`س و ر:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:23 `سُورَة`, `مِثْل`; 2:24 `نَار`; 2:26 `مَثَلًا`; 2:37 `كَلِمَات`; 2:39 `آيَات`.
- Synthesis: Word, analogy, beacon, and bounded surah are complementary forms of indication: semantic, figurative, visual, and textual.

### S4. P2 (2:21-39) - Fabricated utterance tested for truth
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A speaker constructs a claim, attributes it as a position, and exposes it to a test of truthfulness.
- Active motifs: inventing false speech (`خ ل ق:B007/m01`); contrived fabrication (`ف ع ل:B004/m01`); truthfulness of a statement (`ص د ق:B001/m01`); utterance as belief or position (`ق و ل:B013/m01`); statement defining its object (`ق و ل:B016/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:21, 2:29 `خَلَق`; 2:23, 2:31 `صَادِقِين`; 2:24 `تَفْعَلُوا`; 2:25-26, 2:30-38 forms of `قَال`, `قُل`.
- Synthesis: Fabrication and truth are opposed outcomes of the same constructive speech act: a claim is made, given doctrinal shape, and judged by whether it corresponds to what it defines.

### S5. P3 (2:40-61) - Prophetic elevation and counterfeit claim
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A bearer of divine report occupies an elevated role, while a counterfeit claimant conceals truth and resists proper allegiance.
- Active motifs: prophet bearing divine news (`ن ب ء:B003/m01`); false claim to prophecy (`ن ب ء:B004/m01`); elevation and high position (`ن ب و:B001/m01`); aversion and refusal to comply (`ن ب و:B004/m01`); covering truth (`ك ف ر:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:41, 2:61 forms of `كَفَر`; 2:61 `النَّبِيِّين`.
- Synthesis: Height and message define the legitimate role; false assertion, concealment, and noncompliance define its counterfeit.

### S6. P4 (2:62-74) - Color, contrast, and marking
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A surface acquires a vivid base color, receives a contrasting mark, and can be intentionally dyed.
- Active motifs: yellow coloration (`ص ف ر:B001/m01`); intense yellow (`ف ق ع:B005/m01`); surface complexion (`ل و ن:B001/m01`); taking on a new color (`ل و ن:B003/m01`); mark contrasting with the dominant color (`و ش ي:B001/m01`); pouring dye onto cloth (`س ق ي:B009/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:69 `صَفْرَاء`, `فَاقِع`, `لَوْن`; 2:71 `شِيَة`, `تَسْقِي`.
- Synthesis: Hue, saturation, recoloring, contrast mark, and dyeing form a complete surface-treatment scene centered on visible differentiation.

### S7. P5 (2:75-86) - Bloodshed, seizure, and captivity
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: Bodily blood is spilled, persons are seized and bound, and captivity converts violence into controlled possession.
- Active motifs: blood as bodily substance (`د م و:B001/m01`); flowing blood (`د م ي:B001/m01`); blood as support of embodied life (`ن ف س:B004/m01`); binding and imprisonment (`ء س ر:B001/m01`); taking by capture (`ء خ ذ:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:83-84 `أَخَذْنَا`; 2:84 `دِمَاء`, `أَنفُس`; 2:85 `أُسَارَى`, `أَنفُس`.
- Synthesis: Flowing blood marks bodily violation; seizure and binding then transform exposed persons into captives within a coercive social frame.

### S8. P5 (2:75-86) - Divergence into exile and hostility
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Former associates take opposing routes, transgress limits, and subject one another to defeat and displacement from home.
- Active motifs: disastrous turn or defeat (`د و ر:B004/m01`); parties taking divergent paths (`خ ل ف:B004/m01`); hostile transgression beyond a limit (`ع د و:B001/m01`); distance produced by enmity (`ب ع د:B010/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:75 `بَعْد`; 2:80 `يُخْلِف`; 2:84-85 `دِيَار`; 2:85 `عُدْوَان`.
- Synthesis: Divergent paths become social separation, then hostile excess, defeat, and removal from dwellings.

### S9. P6 (2:87-103) - Separation engineered into harm
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A widening gap permits an adversarial force to divert parties, create injury, and leave them under compulsion until a separating purification occurs.
- Active motifs: widened distance (`ب ي ن:B006/m01`); distance and severance (`ش ط ن:B001/m01`); turning away from the right (`ف ت ن:B003/m01`); reciprocal injury (`ض ر ر:B002/m01`); constraining necessity (`ض ر ر:B003/m01`); purification from mixture (`خ ل ص:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:87, 2:92, 2:97, 2:99, 2:102 forms of `بَيِّن`, `بَيْن`; 2:94 `خَالِصَة`; 2:102 `الشَّيَاطِين`, `فِتْنَة`, `ضَارِّين`, `يَضُر`.
- Synthesis: Separation is both method and result: a gap is opened, diversion enters it, harm constrains the parties, and purification would be the operation that removes the intrusive mixture.

### S10. P6 (2:87-103) - Front, rear, and positional sequence
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A body or message is located between what lies before it and what remains behind, creating a directed sequence.
- Active motifs: position between the hands or directly before (`ي د ي:B008/m01`); rear side that may also be construed relative to the observer (`و ر ي:B006/m01`); rear or delayed position (`ء خ ر:B003/m01`); front rank and leading edge (`ق د م:B007/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:91, 2:101 `وَرَاء`; 2:94, 2:102 `آخِرَة`; 2:95 `قَدَّمَتْ`, `أَيْدِي`; 2:97 `يَدَيْ`.
- Synthesis: Front and rear are relational rather than absolute. The observer's position orders an item between prior and subsequent locations.

### S11. P7 (2:104-121) - Decree bringing a measured thing into existence
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An intended matter is measured, deliberated, decisively enacted, and thereby established in existence.
- Active motifs: perfected execution of an act (`ق ض ي:B005/m01`); quantity reaching its limit (`ق د ر:B001/m01`); deliberative determination (`ق د ر:B005/m01`); measuring and enforcing a decree (`م ن ي:B001/m01`); established existence (`و ج د:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:106, 2:109 `قَدِير`; 2:110 `تَجِدُوا`; 2:111 `أَمَانِيّ`; 2:117 `قَضَى`.
- Synthesis: Measure and deliberation precede decisive execution; the outcome is not merely commanded but made stably existent.

### S12. P7 (2:104-121) - Obstruction and coercive restraint
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A barrier stands between an actor and a desired act, withholds a right, and presses the actor through inducement or forced abstention.
- Active motifs: barrier preventing access to an aim (`م ن ع:B002/m01`); withholding a right (`ظ ل م:B008/m01`); restraint and forced abstention (`ع ذ ب:B003/m01`); solicitation toward an act (`ر و د:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:108 `تُرِيدُوا`; 2:104, 2:114 `عَذَاب`; 2:114 `أَظْلَم`, `مَنَع`.
- Synthesis: The scene combines negative and positive pressure: access is blocked and a right withheld, while the subject is simultaneously pressed toward or away from action.

### S13. P8 (2:122-141) - Unity enacted as a religious way
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A community acknowledges one deity and embodies that unity through submission, worship, rite, and a followed way.
- Active motifs: divine oneness without partner (`و ح د:B004/m01`); numerical and ontological unity (`ء ح د:B001/m01`); deity as object of worship (`ء ل ه:B001/m01`); obedience and submission (`د ي ن:B001/m01`); followed religious way (`م ل ل:B003/m01`); ritual devotion (`ن س ك:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:126, 2:132-133, 2:136-140 forms of `اللَّه`, `إِلَه`; 2:128 `مَنَاسِك`; 2:130, 2:135 `مِلَّة`; 2:132 `دِّين`; 2:133 `وَاحِدًا`; 2:136 `أَحَد`.
- Synthesis: Unity is not an abstract count alone. It is realized in directed worship, submission, ritual practice, and a shared path.

### S14. P8 (2:122-141) - Presence at the terminal moment
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Witnesses gather near a person at death, observe the transfer, and orient the departing life toward its final place.
- Active motifs: nearness and direct presence (`ح ض ر:B001/m01`); arrival of death or harm (`ح ض ر:B009/m01`); presence with observation (`ش ه د:B001/m01`); final place of settlement (`ص ي ر:B007/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:126 `مَصِير`; 2:133 `حَضَر`, `شُهَدَاء`; 2:140 `شَهَادَة`.
- Synthesis: Death is staged socially: participants draw near, witness the final charge, and face the transition toward a settled destination.

### S15. P9 (2:142-152) - Racing toward the right course
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Competitors identify the right direction, enter a race toward it, and stake themselves on reaching it first.
- Active motifs: advancing ahead in a race (`س ب ق:B001/m01`); stake placed on a contest (`س ب ق:B002/m01`); gentle direction toward the way (`ه د ي:B001/m01`); course and intended bearing (`ه د ي:B002/m01`); correct aspect of a matter (`و ج ه:B008/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:142-143, 2:150 forms of `هَدَى`; 2:144, 2:148-150 forms of `وَجْه`; 2:148 `اسْتَبِقُوا`.
- Synthesis: Correct bearing gives the race a destination, while precedence and stake make pursuit urgent and consequential.

### S16. P10 (2:153-177) - A call without receptive hearing
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A raised call reaches the physical ear but fails to become comprehended sound, leaving the hearer deaf and unseeing.
- Active motifs: raised voice and call (`ن د و:B002/m01`); auditory perception (`س م ع:B001/m01`); ear as hearing organ (`س م ع:B002/m01`); deafness and nonresponse (`ص م م:B001/m01`); blindness (`ع م ي:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:171 `نِدَاء`, `يَسْمَع`, `صُمّ`, `عُمْي`.
- Synthesis: Signal, organ, and failed uptake are all present. The call exists acoustically, but no intelligible reception or orientation follows.

### S17. P10 (2:153-177) - Gambling apparatus and assigned lots
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Marked arrows are gathered in a vessel, supervised by an appointed watcher, and distributed as lots in a game.
- Active motifs: vessel gathering gambling arrows (`ر ب ب:B010/m01`); supervisor and arrow of the gambling game (`ر ق ب:B006/m01`); fifth gambling arrow (`ن ف س:B016/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:155 `أَنفُس`; 2:157 `رَب`; 2:177 `رِقَاب`.
- Synthesis: Container, official, and specifically ranked lot form a compact operational scene for drawing shares by chance.

### S18. P11 (2:178-203) - Bodily intimacy and mutual covering
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Two partners meet skin to skin, enter mutual bodily association, and become reciprocal covering and nourishment.
- Active motifs: contact of skin with skin (`ب ش ر:B003/m01`); wholeness joining outer and inner person (`ب ش ر:B008/m01`); intimate association and cohabitation (`ل ب س:B004/m01`); kiss of the mouth (`ق ب ل:B006/m01`); mouth-to-mouth feeding (`ط ع م:B013/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:183, 2:198 `قَبْل`; 2:184 `طَعَام`; 2:187 `بَاشِرُوا`, `تُبَاشِرُوهُن`, `لِبَاس`.
- Synthesis: Contact, cohabitation, covering, kiss, and feeding form a reciprocal bodily scene rather than a generic relation of marriage.

### S19. P11 (2:178-203) - Speech delivered to its hearer
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A statement is composed and clarified, spoken with enough force and precision to reach its listener, and gathered into recitation.
- Active motifs: conveying sound to the ear (`ء د ي:B007/m01`); decisive communication and instruction (`ق ض ي:B002/m01`); eloquence that reaches its aim (`ب ل غ:B004/m01`); exposing meaning by speech or sign (`ب ي ن:B005/m01`); gathering words in reading (`ق ر ء:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:178 `أَدَاء`; 2:182, 2:185, 2:187-188 forms of `بَيْن`; 2:185 `قُرْآن`; 2:196 `يَبْلُغ`; 2:200 `قَضَيْتُم`.
- Synthesis: Expression is modeled as delivery: language is assembled, clarified, propelled toward an aim, and received as an audible charge.

### S20. P12 (2:204-220) - Inflated self and constricted breath
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Self-magnification swells an inward disposition while breath and chest tighten under the strain.
- Active motifs: magnifying oneself (`ع ج ب:B002/m01`); force and disposition of the self (`ن ف س:B014/m01`); breath issuing from the body (`ن ف س:B001/m01`); chest spasm or death-rattle (`ف و ق:B010/m01`); heart as inward seat (`ق ل ب:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:204 `يُعْجِبُ`, `قَلْب`; 2:207 `نَفْس`; 2:212 `فَوْق`.
- Synthesis: Pride is given a physiology: an enlarged self occupies the interior while breath shortens and the chest contracts around it.

### S21. P12 (2:204-220) - Kin mixed into a household
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Non-biological dependents are brought into fraternal proximity, where mixing can either corrupt relations or be repaired.
- Active motifs: sibling relation (`ء خ و:B001/m01`); blood kinship (`ق ر ب:B003/m01`); protected close relatives and women (`ح ر م:B011/m01`); mixing that disrupts right order (`خ ل ط:B003/m01`); repair opposed to corruption (`ص ل ح:B001/m01`); departure from sound order (`ف س د:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:205, 2:220 forms of `فَسَاد`, `مُفْسِد`; 2:214-215 `قَرِيب`, `أَقْرَبِين`; 2:217 `حَرَام`; 2:220 `إِخْوَان`, `تُخَالِطُوا`, `إِصْلَاح`, `مُصْلِح`.
- Synthesis: Household incorporation is a social mixing operation. Fraternal status can absorb the dependent, but the quality of mixing determines whether the result is corruption or repair.

### S22. P13 (2:221-242) - Knotted and released speech
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Speech is held as if by a knot, then clarified into an utterance that another person can understand.
- Active motifs: tongue tied by a speech-knot (`ع ق د:B007/m01`); tongue held back (`ع ق ل:B003/m01`); spoken utterance (`ق و ل:B001/m01`); meaning exposed through speech or sign (`ب ي ن:B005/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:221, 2:230, 2:232, 2:237, 2:242 forms of `يُبَيِّن`, `بَيْن`; 2:235, 2:237 `عُقْدَة`; 2:235 `قَوْلًا`; 2:242 `تَعْقِلُون`.
- Synthesis: The knot and held tongue describe obstruction at the organ of speech; utterance and clarification describe its successful release into shared meaning.

### S23. P14 (2:243-253) - River crossing as a test of intake
- Reading type: surface-primary
- Scene or process: A group crosses a river under a rule limiting how much water may be taken by hand or vessel.
- Active motifs: drinking liquid (`ش ر ب:B001/m01`); drinking place or implement (`ش ر ب:B004/m01`); crossing through a place (`ج و ز:B002/m01`); lifting a portion by hand or scoop (`غ ر ف:B001/m01`); river cut by running water (`ن ه ر:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:249 `جَاوَزَه`, `نَهَر`, `شَرِب`, `اغْتَرَف`, `غُرْفَة`, `يَد`.
- Synthesis: River, crossing, intake rule, hand-scoop, and measured portion form a single trial in which bodily thirst is governed during passage.

### S24. P14 (2:243-253) - Life spared, taken, and evidenced
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A life may be extinguished, preserved from killing, or identified as dead through the trace left behind.
- Active motifs: loss of vital force (`م و ت:B001/m01`); ascertainment that hunted prey has died (`م و ت:B014/m01`); sparing and preserving life (`ح ي ي:B006/m01`); death expressed as release from toil (`ر و ح:B016/m01`); surviving trace after departure (`ت ر ك:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:243 `مَوْت`, `مُوتُوا`, `أَحْيَاهُم`; 2:248 `تَرَكَ`; 2:253 `رُوح`, `اقْتَتَلُوا`.
- Synthesis: Life and death are framed as a decision with evidence: killing removes force, sparing retains it, and remaining traces disclose what occurred.

### S25. P15 (2:254-266) - Administration of charitable return
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An officeholder oversees a monetary gift, assigns compensation for work, and distributes an apportioned return.
- Active motifs: administrative office over a group (`س ع ي:B003/m01`); charitable payment (`ص د ق:B006/m01`); taking charge of an affair (`و ل ي:B003/m01`); reward assigned for work (`ج ع ل:B005/m01`); apportioned gift (`ر ز ق:B001/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:254 `رَزَقْنَاكُم`; 2:257 `وَلِيّ`, `أَوْلِيَاء`; 2:259-260 `نَجْعَل`, `اجْعَل`; 2:260 `سَعْيًا`; 2:263-264 `صَدَقَة`, `صَدَقَات`.
- Synthesis: Gift, administrator, assigned wage, and distribution form an institutional scene in which charity is managed rather than merely handed over.

### S26. P15 (2:254-266) - Consolidated support for rule
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: A fixed base gathers and stabilizes collective power, supports an affair, and strengthens sovereign command.
- Active motifs: compacted gathering and stability (`ك ر س:B001/m01`); fixed foundation (`ك ر س:B002/m01`); support on which authority stands (`ع ر ش:B006/m01`); strengthening and reinforcement (`ع ز ز:B004/m01`); sovereignty and dominion (`م ل ك:B003/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:255 `كُرْسِيّ`; 2:258 `مُلْك`; 2:259 `عُرُوش`; 2:260 `عَزِيز`.
- Synthesis: Foundation, gathered mass, supporting frame, reinforcement, and dominion assemble a structural image of rule made stable.

### S27. P16 (2:267-286) - Capacity enclosed by burden
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A person's available room is measured, then narrowed by an imposed load that must not exceed the person's power.
- Active motifs: openness opposed to constriction (`و س ع:B001/m01`); capacity and endurance (`و س ع:B002/m01`); interval, room, and respite (`ن ف س:B015/m01`); imposed hardship or right (`ك ل ف:B003/m01`); heavy burden carried (`ء ص ر:B004/m01`); ability to carry with difficulty (`ط و ق:B002/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:268 `وَاسِع`; 2:272, 2:281, 2:284, 2:286 `أَنفُس`, `نَفْس`; 2:286 `يُكَلِّف`, `وُسْع`, `إِصْرًا`, `طَاقَة`.
- Synthesis: Capacity is spatialized as room around the self. Burden occupies that room, and justice requires that the load remain within its boundary.

### S28. P16 (2:267-286) - Stored water and connected channels
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Water is conducted along a channel, gathered in basin and pool, drawn from a well, and released into a river.
- Active motifs: channeling water along a route (`ء ت ي:B004/m01`); reservoir collecting water (`ء ج ل:B007/m01`); pool where water gathers (`ج ي ء:B002/m01`); river cutting the earth (`ن ه ر:B001/m01`); well as a water source (`ق ل ب:B007/m01`); abundant collected water (`ع ل م:B005/m01`).
- Ayah anchors: 2:269, 2:271, 2:277 forms of `آتَى`; 2:274 `النَّهَار`; 2:275 `جَاء`; 2:282 `أَجَل`, forms of `عَلِم`; 2:283 `قَلْب`.
- Synthesis: Conduit, reservoir, pool, well, accumulated water, and river form a complete hydrological storage-and-release network.

## Cross-Pericope Channels

### X1. Water from sky to body, field, and store
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P10 (2:153-177), P12 (2:204-220), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Water moves through a linked system of source, descent, opening, channel, reception, storage, and use.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; cloud and rain in P2 and P10 descend to ground, P4 opens conduits, P12 carries relief along routes, P14 makes a river a traversed intake point, P15 tests the receiving substrate, and P16 gathers water in basin, pool, well, and river. P3 supplies bodily intake within the same downstream sequence.
- Local findings joined: P2 “Rain animating the ground”; P3 “Water between sweetness and aversion”; P4 “Fissure, channel, and released water” and “Incision and made channels”; P10 “Water moving from atmosphere to land”; P12 “Rain-supported passage”; P14 “River crossing as a test of intake”; P15 “Rain on an exposed surface”; P16 “Stored water and connected channels”.
- Synthesis: These scenes form one hydrological progression without erasing their different operations. Water is formed above, descends, finds or makes a passage, gathers or runs, encounters a receptive or resistant surface, and finally sustains land, travel, and bodies.

### X2. Palm maturation as a model of increase
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P13 (2:221-242), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Legitimate increase develops through sustained stages from hidden support to dependent shoot, mature stand, and productive flourishing.
- Bridge: causal sequence followed by analogical extension; P1 supplies hidden roots, core, tree, and blossom, P13 supplies the nursery of dependent palm shoots, P15 supplies the cultivated palm garden, and P16 extends nurture and biological increase to financial growth.
- Local findings joined: P1 “Hidden palm growth”; P13 “Horticultural nursery”; P15 “Cultivated palm garden”; P16 “Nurtured increase”.
- Synthesis: The repeated object and developmental roles create a continuous plant life-cycle. Financial increase enters only at the final analogical step, where proper growth remains something tended and brought to completion rather than extracted instantaneously.

### X3. Cultivation, damage, and return
- Pericopes spanned: P4 (2:62-74), P12 (2:204-220), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: An input produces return only through a workable substrate, directed labor, and preservation from destructive or nullifying operations.
- Bridge: repeated scene signature with contrast; P4 joins traction, disturbed soil, seed, and irrigation, P12 contrasts labor and repair with corruption and field destruction, P15 contrasts a yielding garden with washed or disabled ground, and P16 transfers the same input-growth-return structure to expenditure and financial increase.
- Local findings joined: P4 “Bovine traction and field work”; P12 “Workers shaped by repeated action” and “Field damaged or restored”; P15 “Substrate that yields or nullifies return”; P16 “Nurtured increase”.
- Synthesis: Worker, input, substrate, operation, and outcome recur in each scene. Yield is the result of coordinated cultivation; corruption, hardness, or nullification breaks that sequence and prevents return.

### X4. From utterance to accountable public record
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P11 (2:178-203), P14 (2:243-253), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Information becomes binding when it is made intelligible, transmitted, tested, publicly known, and fixed in a durable form.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; P2 forms sign and claim, P5 gives the claim a hand-produced record, P6 supplies vocal relay and recognition, P7 tests speech by proof, P8 teaches signs, P9 makes knowledge public through recitation and testimony, P11 delivers clarified speech, P14 establishes truth through deliberation, and P16 fixes the claim by writing, witnesses, performance, and pledge.
- Local findings joined: P2 “Sign, utterance, and beacon” and “Fabricated utterance tested for truth”; P5 “Hand-produced record and claim”; P6 “Message reception and relay”; P7 “Presented speech and evidence”; P8 “Signs made intelligible”; P9 “Public transmission of known truth”; P11 “Speech delivered to its hearer”; P14 “Deliberation before commission”; P16 “Written, witnessed, and pledged transfer”.
- Synthesis: The bridge is an evidentiary chain, not a general communication theme. A sign or utterance moves through sender, hearer, examiner, teacher, witness, writer, and obligated party until its content becomes publicly accountable.

### X5. Making a route legible and traversable
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P7 (2:104-121), P9 (2:142-152), P12 (2:204-220), and P14 (2:243-253).
- Shared semantic invariant: Movement succeeds when a route is disclosed, marked, oriented, protected from diversion, and crossed under a governing rule.
