- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; P1 supplies intermittent visibility for walking, P7 supplies marked roads, branches, guide, and pursuer, P9 supplies facing, axis, reversal, and race, P12 supplies obstruction and diversion, and P14 supplies route-governing leadership and a controlled river crossing.
- Local findings joined: P1 “Intermittent illumination”; P7 “Marked routes and pursuit”; P9 “Orientation by a governing axis” and “Racing toward the right course”; P12 “Routes under obstruction and aid”; P14 “Prophetic and royal direction” and “River crossing as a test of intake”.
- Synthesis: Light first makes movement possible; marks and a guide then identify the course; an axis aligns the traveler; obstacles test fidelity to it; and crossing demonstrates whether the route has actually been followed.

### X6. Custody and discharge of binding obligation
- Pericopes spanned: P5 (2:75-86), P8 (2:122-141), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: A binding claim persists by being preserved, conveyed to a responsible party, regulated by terms, and finally retained, released, or discharged.
- Bridge: social-frame extension and role progression; P5 establishes protected covenant and accountable record, P8 carries an entrusted charge into a later generation, P11 transfers testament and liability across death, P13 shows a contractual bond formed and released under appointed terms, and P16 secures debt through surety, writing, witness, performance, and pledge.
- Local findings joined: P5 “Bonds that obligate and protect” and “Recorded words in exchange”; P8 “Covenant carried as legacy”; P11 “Transfer under protection”; P13 “Binding and releasing a union” and “Delay until an appointed term”; P16 “Recorded obligation and guarantee”.
- Synthesis: Covenant, testament, marriage, and debt remain distinct institutions. Their bridge is the custody mechanics of obligation: creation, preservation, transfer, temporal regulation, security, and lawful release.

### X7. Dependency answered by transferred care
- Pericopes spanned: P5 (2:75-86), P8 (2:122-141), P10 (2:153-177), P13 (2:221-242), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: A dependent person is sustained when a responsible caregiver or community recognizes need and transfers protection, nourishment, or property.
- Bridge: repeated scene signature and role progression; P13 supplies biological dependence in gestation and nursing, P8 locates the dependent within household and descent, P5 exposes interrupted guardianship in orphanhood, P10 redistributes provision across weakened ties, and P16 recognizes concealed poverty and releases voluntary relief.
- Local findings joined: P5 “Kinship and interrupted care”; P8 “Household and descent”; P10 “Care distributed through the social body”; P13 “Dependent life from gestation to separation”; P16 “Need answered by voluntary relief”.
- Synthesis: Caregiver, dependent, needed resource, transfer, and sustained outcome recur across the five scenes. The progression moves from bodily dependence to household responsibility and then to communal repair when ordinary guardianship or means are absent.

### X8. Action bounded by term, measure, and capacity
- Pericopes spanned: P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: A valid action must occur within a temporal boundary and must not exceed a measured bodily, material, or legal capacity.
- Bridge: repeated scene signature and causal sequence; P11 defines recurring times and terminal limits, P13 joins appointed terms to calibrated burden, P14 tests a group by a measured intake while endurance is under pressure, and P16 fixes a debt term while enclosing burden within personal capacity.
- Local findings joined: P11 “Time bounded by thresholds”; P13 “Measured delay and capacity”; P14 “River crossing as a test of intake” and “Force, endurance, and aid”; P16 “Recorded obligation and guarantee” and “Capacity enclosed by burden”.
- Synthesis: Time, quantity, intake, and load are different measures, but each regulates action by the same sequence: establish a limit, approach it, test available capacity, and stop or discharge at the proper point.

### X9. Vital force lost, preserved, and restored
- Pericopes spanned: P6 (2:87-103), P10 (2:153-177), P14 (2:243-253), and P15 (2:254-266).
- Shared semantic invariant: Life is an animating force whose removal produces stillness, whose protection prevents extinction, and whose return reverses apparent finality.
- Bridge: contrast and reversal; P6 models animation through spirit and breath and extinction through their loss, P10 extends life-giving force to revived land, P14 contrasts killing with sparing and evidencing death, and P15 stages sleep-like stillness, death, reassurance, and reanimation.
- Local findings joined: P6 “Life-force entering and leaving the body”; P10 “Descent, collection, and terrestrial life”; P14 “Life spared, taken, and evidenced”; P15 “Stillness, death, and return to life”.
- Synthesis: The stable contrast is animation versus cessation; the decisive reversal is restoration. Body and landscape remain separate patients, but both participate in the same loss-preservation-revival structure.

### X10. Qualified authority becoming administration
- Pericopes spanned: P7 (2:104-121), P14 (2:243-253), and P15 (2:254-266).
- Shared semantic invariant: Authority is legitimate when fitness precedes commission, judgment directs collective action, and stable office administers entrusted resources.
- Bridge: role progression; P7 defines entitlement, qualification, office, and sovereignty, P14 adds prophetic message, royal direction, deliberation, and judgment, and P15 supplies the structural support of rule and the practical administration of charitable return.
- Local findings joined: P7 “Qualified governance”; P14 “Authority carried by message and judgment”; P15 “Consolidated support for rule” and “Administration of charitable return”.
- Synthesis: The progression runs from qualified officeholder to commissioned judge and then to durable administration. Power alone does not bridge the scenes; fitness, knowledgeable direction, and stewardship do.

### X11. Provision circulating through changing roles
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P5 (2:75-86), P10 (2:153-177), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: A material share changes social role as it is allotted, consumed, exchanged, administered, and released toward need.
- Bridge: role progression; P2 turns allotment into bodily substance, P3 makes food selectable and exchangeable, P5 supplies acquisition, handover, and price, P10 moves provision from bodies to vulnerable households, P15 gives charity an administrative frame, and P16 contrasts nurtured circulation with extraction while directing surplus to poverty.
- Local findings joined: P2 “Allotment becoming bodily substance”; P3 “Choosing and exchanging food”; P5 “Acquisition, handover, and price”; P10 “Provision incorporated by bodies and households”; P15 “Administration of charitable return”; P16 “Growth through financial transfer” and “Need answered by voluntary relief”.
- Synthesis: The bridge follows the object rather than grouping economic topics. The same transferred share changes function as food, merchandise, household support, managed charity, productive expenditure, or relief.

### X12. Bodily orientation enacting allegiance
- Pericopes spanned: P3 (2:40-61), P8 (2:122-141), and P9 (2:142-152).
- Shared semantic invariant: Allegiance becomes publicly embodied by lowering, aligning, and directing the body.
- Bridge: repeated scene signature with role progression; P3 lowers head and frame in bowing and prostration, P8 joins that posture to purification, reconciliation, and submission, and P9 turns the face and communal body toward a governing direction.
- Local findings joined: P3 “Bodily yielding and abasement”; P8 “Purification through posture and peace” and “Unity enacted as a religious way”; P9 “Face aligned to a direction”.
- Synthesis: Bowed frame, prostrating body, and directed face are materially different postures, but each converts an inward relation into visible alignment.

### X13. Receptive boundaries and blocked transfer
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P4 (2:62-74), P6 (2:87-103), and P15 (2:254-266).
- Shared semantic invariant: A signal or substance produces effect only when the boundary it meets opens, admits, or transmits it.
- Bridge: functional analogy with contrast and reversal; P1 contrasts admitted sound and light with sealed hearing and sight, P4 contrasts hardened heart-stone with stone that fissures and releases water, P6 places imbibed understanding inside the heart, and P15 contrasts receptive soil with a hard surface that sheds rain and nullifies return.
- Local findings joined: P1 “Sensory ingress and closure” and “Intermittent illumination”; P4 “Hard matter opened to flow”; P6 “Understanding imbibed into the heart”; P15 “Rain on an exposed surface” and “Benefit rendered void”.
- Synthesis: Ear, eye, heart, stone, and soil are not merged as objects. They share a boundary function: opening permits reception or release, while closure leaves the arriving force ineffective.

### X14. Hostility escalating from separation to open combat
- Pericopes spanned: P5 (2:75-86), P7 (2:104-121), and P14 (2:243-253).
- Shared semantic invariant: Conflict intensifies as affiliation breaks, rights are obstructed, persons are coerced, and opposed groups finally enter exposed combat.
- Bridge: causal escalation and role progression; P5 moves from divergent paths and hostile excess to bloodshed, captivity, and exile, P7 supplies obstruction and coercive restraint, and P14 assembles opposed sides, force, endurance, killing, and aid in open battle.
- Local findings joined: P5 “Bloodshed, seizure, and captivity” and “Divergence into exile and hostility”; P7 “Obstruction and coercive restraint”; P14 “Mobilized contest” and “Life spared, taken, and evidenced”.
- Synthesis: The channel is an escalation sequence rather than a generic violence category. Broken affiliation changes parties into opponents, coercion restricts their agency, and organized confrontation converts hostility into battle.

### X15. Gestation passing through birth into postpartum recovery
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P2 (2:21-39), P5 (2:75-86), P8 (2:122-141), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Enclosed life approaches a bodily threshold, exits under labor, leaves diagnostic traces, and changes the mother's condition afterward.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; the fetus occupies the womb, nears delivery, is received at birth, and is followed by afterbirth, blood, or uterine pain.
- Active bridge motifs: fetus hidden in the abdomen (`ج ن ن:B007/m01`); female womb as container (`ر ح م:B003/m01`); nearness of labor (`ق ر ب:B012/m01`); occurrence of birth (`و ل د:B003/m01`); afterbirth membrane (`ح و ل:B008/m01`); birth trace or discharge (`ش ه د:B006/m01`); postpartum uterine pain (`ر ح م:B004/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P5 “Kinship and interrupted care”; P8 “Household and descent”; P13 “Dependent life from gestation to separation”.
- Synthesis: This physiological sequence remains distinct from X7's social transfer of care. Its invariant is passage through the maternal boundary and the bodily aftermath that evidences delivery.

### X16. Household continuity through descent, testament, and estate
- Pericopes spanned: P3 (2:40-61), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), and P14 (2:243-253).
- Shared semantic invariant: A household persists when membership, property, and instruction pass from an earlier bearer to a later kin group.
- Bridge: role progression; family and household establish the receiving group, testament preserves intention, death creates an estate, and inheritance installs a successor.
- Active bridge motifs: household membership (`ء ه ل:B001/m01`); household and dependents (`ب ي ت:B002/m01`); clan group (`ع ش ر:B013/m01`); estate left by the dead (`ت ر ك:B006/m01`); inheritance transferred to a successor (`و ر ث:B001/m01`); close lineage segment (`ف ص ل:B009/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P8 “Lineage as transmitted obligation”; P11 “Testament securing kin after death”; P13 “Dependent life from gestation to separation”.
- Synthesis: The bridge follows continuity of the household rather than obligation in general. Persons belong, a predecessor departs, and kin receive both material residue and transmitted charge.

### X17. Marriage from eligibility to union, waiting, and release
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P5 (2:75-86), P8 (2:122-141), P11 (2:178-203), P12 (2:204-220), P13 (2:221-242), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Marital status changes through recognized entry, embodied partnership, regulated waiting, dissolution, and possible return.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; absence of a spouse permits courtship, contract creates the pair, intimacy enacts union, a waiting term governs transition, and divorce or return changes the relation again.
- Active bridge motifs: being without spouse (`خ ل و:B009/m01`); marriage proposal (`خ ط ب:B002/m01`); marriage contract (`ن ك ح:B002/m01`); intimate cohabitation (`ل ب س:B004/m01`); marital waiting period (`ر ب ص:B003/m01`); release from marriage (`ط ل ق:B002/m01`); marital return (`ر ج ع:B004/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P11 “Bodily intimacy and mutual covering”; P13 “Binding and releasing a union” and “Delay until an appointed term”.
- Synthesis: Contract, intimacy, waiting, divorce, and return are successive legal and bodily states of one relationship. They are not collapsed into the broader custody mechanics of X6.

### X18. Captivity reversed through ransom and release
- Pericopes spanned: P3 (2:40-61), P5 (2:75-86), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Control over a person is materialized by seizure and binding, then reversed by substitution, payment, or formal emancipation.
- Bridge: contrast and causal reversal; capture produces the prisoner, restraint maintains custody, ransom or an emancipation contract supplies the releasing condition, and unbinding restores movement or status.
- Active bridge motifs: seizure as captivity (`ء خ ذ:B003/m01`); binding and imprisonment (`ء س ر:B001/m01`); restraint by tether (`و ث ق:B003/m01`); ransom of a prisoner (`ف د ي:B002/m01`); release from a bond (`ط ل ق:B001/m01`); freedom opposed to slavery (`ح ر ر:B002/m01`); emancipation contract (`ك ت ب:B005/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P5 “Bloodshed, seizure, and captivity”; P11 “Liability, substitution, and ransom”; P13 “Unbinding, retention, and release”.
- Synthesis: The stable patient is the restrained person. The channel moves from physical possession to a compensatory or contractual reversal that ends custody.

### X19. Wound, treatment, healing, and equivalent redress
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P5 (2:75-86), P7 (2:104-121), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P14 (2:243-253), and P15 (2:254-266).
- Shared semantic invariant: Bodily injury generates observable damage that must be treated physically and answered proportionately in law.
- Bridge: causal sequence followed by social-frame extension; a wound opens and bleeds, probing or tissue closure treats it, while retaliation or compensation prevents the injury from becoming an unanswered loss.
- Active bridge motifs: bodily abscess or open sore (`خ ر ج:B004/m01`); flowing blood (`د م ي:B001/m01`); bodily wound (`ك ل م:B003/m01`); probing and treating a head wound (`ح ج ج:B004/m01`); flesh closing over a wound (`ل ح م:B008/m01`); blood left without compensation (`ب ط ل:B006/m01`); equivalent retaliation (`ق ص ص:B003/m01`); execution of redress (`ص ب ر:B012/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P5 “Bloodshed, seizure, and captivity”; P7 “Word as intelligible or injurious mark”; P14 “Mobilized contest”; P15 “Benefit rendered void”.
- Synthesis: Medical repair and legal redress are not the same operation. Their bridge is restoration after injury: one closes damaged tissue, while the other closes an outstanding claim.

### X20. Fear becoming vigilance, defense, and security
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P9 (2:142-152), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Anticipated harm reorganizes attention and action until danger is repelled and the heart can settle.
- Bridge: causal sequence with contrast; alarm contracts the heart, vigilance identifies danger, defensive force turns it away, and security or tranquility reverses the initial state.
- Active bridge motifs: fear of expected harm (`خ و ف:B001/m01`); heart divided by fear (`ف ر ق:B009/m01`); alert precaution (`ح ذ ر:B001/m01`); defensive repulsion (`د ر ء:B001/m01`); protection by pushing harm away (`د ف ع:B001/m01`); security and trust (`ء م ن:B001/m01`); calm after disturbance (`ط م ء ن:B001/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P1 “Lightning-governed movement”; P9 “Orientation by a governing axis”; P14 “Force, endurance, and aid”; P15 “Stillness, death, and return to life”.
- Synthesis: Fear is retained as an initiating state, not grouped loosely with conflict. The channel is the conversion of alarm into guarded action and then into settled safety.

### X21. Anger heated into confrontation
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P12 (2:204-220), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Inner agitation behaves like fire: it is stirred, grows hot and visible, and can pass into overt hostility.
- Bridge: functional analogy and causal escalation; resentment is figured as ignition and facial heat, agitation is stirred like embers, and the resulting surge becomes quarrel or war.
- Active bridge motifs: wrath seeking retaliation (`غ ض ب:B001/m01`); anger surging toward confrontation (`ث و ر:B003/m01`); face blazing with anger (`ج ح م:B004/m01`); agitation and headlong intensity (`ش ر ي:B008/m01`); stirring fire or war (`ح ر ث:B005/m01`); provoking hostility (`ح ر ب:B003/m01`); mutual combat (`ق ت ل:B011/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P1 “Kindled light and visual exposure”; P5 “Divergence into exile and hostility”; P12 “Inflated self and constricted breath”; P14 “Mobilized contest”.
- Synthesis: The bridge is a heat-and-motion transformation, not a general association of fire with violence. Internal pressure becomes visible heat and then outward attack.

### X22. The heart hardened, instructed, alarmed, and reassured
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P9 (2:142-152), P12 (2:204-220), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: The heart is a mutable interior whose condition determines whether knowledge, fear, reflection, or reassurance can take hold.
- Bridge: same-patient transformation with contrasts; hardness blocks reception, imbibed understanding enters, fear divides, reflection turns the matter repeatedly, and tranquility settles the same interior.
- Active bridge motifs: heart as inward organ and faculty (`ق ل ب:B001/m01`); coarsening of the heart (`ق س و:B002/m01`); understanding as imbibed intake (`ش ر ب:B011/m01`); heart divided by fear (`ف ر ق:B009/m01`); reflective turning within (`ف ك ر:B001/m01`); insight of the heart (`ب ص ر:B002/m01`); tranquility after agitation (`ط م ء ن:B001/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P1 “Sensory ingress and closure”; P4 “Hardened stone and heart”; P6 “Understanding imbibed into the heart”; P12 “Inflated self and constricted breath”; P15 “The heart seeing and thinking”.
- Synthesis: These are different states and operations of one patient. Their sequence explains how the heart can obstruct, absorb, test, or stabilize what reaches it.

### X23. Cleansing by separation, washing, and moral repair
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P6 (2:87-103), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Purity is produced by removing an adherent stain, separating from corruption, or restoring a sound state.
- Bridge: repeated operation with social and moral extensions; water washes the body, separation clears mixture or liability, and purification transfers the same removal pattern to conduct, place, and communal relation.
- Active bridge motifs: washing with water (`ط ه ر:B003/m01`); removal of stain (`ط ه ر:B001/m01`); moral cleansing (`ط ه ر:B005/m01`); purity and soundness (`ز ك و:B002/m01`); separation from fault (`ب ر ء:B002/m01`); purified place (`ق د س:B002/m01`); cleansing from bodily impurity (`ط ي ب:B003/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P6 “Separation engineered into harm”; P8 “Purification through posture and peace”; P9 “Recitation, cleansing, and instruction”; P13 “Womb, cycle, and birth”.
- Synthesis: The recurring mechanism is removal or separation, while the patients remain distinct: body, place, action, and social relation.

### X24. Origination becoming form, image, and sign
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Making becomes legible through a formed appearance that can be reproduced, displayed, and recognized as a sign.
- Bridge: role progression; origination produces a thing, formation gives it perceptible structure, depiction reproduces that structure, and mark or sign lets an observer identify what it represents.
- Active bridge motifs: origination without prior model (`ب د ع:B001/m01`); bringing a thing into existence (`خ ل ق:B002/m01`); completed bodily form (`خ ل ق:B003/m01`); pictured form (`ص و ر:B003/m01`); modeled image (`م ث ل:B008/m01`); analogy made visible (`ض ر ب:B003/m01`); evident sign (`ء ي ي:B003/m01`); distinguishing mark (`ع ل م:B002/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P2 “Sign, utterance, and beacon”; P7 “Decree bringing a measured thing into existence”; P8 “Signs made intelligible”; P15 “The heart seeing and thinking”.
- Synthesis: Creation, depiction, and signification remain different operations. The bridge is the progressive visibility of what has been made.

### X25. Dispute moving through proof to binding judgment
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P5 (2:75-86), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P12 (2:204-220), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: An opposed claim becomes resolvable when argument is tested by evidence and terminated by a discriminating decision.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; entangled speech creates disputants, proof establishes the stronger claim, a judge separates right from falsehood, and writing fixes the result.
- Active bridge motifs: entangled quarrel (`ش ج ر:B002/m01`); prevailing proof (`ح ج ج:B003/m01`); adversarial claimant (`خ ص م:B001/m01`); adjudication between parties (`ح ك م:B002/m01`); verdict separating right from falsehood (`ف ص ل:B002/m01`); demonstration of truth (`ح ق ق:B005/m01`); written imposition of judgment (`ك ت ب:B003/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P2 “Fabricated utterance tested for truth”; P5 “Hand-produced record and claim”; P7 “Presented speech and evidence”; P14 “Deliberation before commission”; P16 “Written, witnessed, and pledged transfer”.
- Synthesis: This is the adversarial branch of X4's evidentiary chain. Its invariant is termination of a contested claim by proof and judgment.

### X26. Migration ending in dwelling and settlement
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P8 (2:122-141), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P12 (2:204-220), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Movement between places reaches completion when an outsider arrives, occupies a site, and converts it into a stable dwelling.
- Bridge: causal sequence and reversal; departure from settled space creates the traveler or stranger, arrival crosses the boundary, and staying reverses displacement into residence.
- Active bridge motifs: departure from settled life (`ب د و:B002/m01`); relocation between places (`ب ق ر:B007/m01`); movement from one land to another (`ن ب ء:B001/m01`); inhabiting a dwelling (`س ك ن:B002/m01`); adherence to a town (`ب ل د:B009/m01`); stable residence (`ق و م:B006/m01`); dwelling or station (`ن ز ل:B003/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P2 “Habitable ordering”; P3 “Descent, unloading, and placement”; P5 “Divergence into exile and hostility”; P8 “Household and descent”; P12 “Routes under obstruction and aid”.
- Synthesis: X5 concerns the legibility of a route; this channel concerns the change of status at its end, from displaced mover to resident.

### X27. Building a shelter from supports, roof, and wall
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), and P15 (2:254-266).
- Shared semantic invariant: Shelter is an object-part assembly in which upright or crossing supports carry an overhead cover while a perimeter encloses the occupied space.
- Bridge: cross-root component assembly; interlocked wood, roof beam, column support, raised canopy, wall, and projecting cover occupy complementary structural roles.
- Active bridge motifs: interlocked supporting wood (`ش ج ر:B004/m01`); roof-bearing beam (`ج و ز:B009/m01`); paired supports for a central post (`ق ر ي:B008/m01`); raised roof or canopy (`ع ر ش:B002/m01`); enclosed precinct (`ح ج ر:B004/m01`); elevated surrounding wall (`س و ر:B002/m01`); projecting shelter (`ك ن ن:B005/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P2 “Floor, canopy, and descent”; P15 “Consolidated support for rule”.
- Synthesis: The channel is architectural rather than metaphorically structural. Each motif supplies a distinct load-bearing, covering, or enclosing function in one built scene.

### X28. Hard material becoming tool, armor, and blade
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P11 (2:178-203), P12 (2:204-220), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Metal's hardness is converted by craft into an implement whose edge acts or whose shell protects.
- Bridge: material-to-function role progression; iron and slag identify the material, the adze gives it a working role, helmet and shield redirect it toward protection, and blade or sheath toward controlled force.
- Active bridge motifs: iron and resistant hardness (`ح د د:B004/m01`); slag expelled in smelting (`خ ب ث:B002/m01`); metal adze for carving (`ق د م:B008/m01`); iron helmet (`ب ي ض:B004/m01`); protective shield (`ج ن ن:B008/m01`); sharpened blade edge (`ح د د:B005/m01`); enclosing sheath (`غ ل ف:B001/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P14 “Mobilized contest”; P15 “Consolidated support for rule”.
- Synthesis: Hardness alone does not define the channel. Its bridge is functional conversion from raw resistant matter into shaped work, protection, or cutting.

### X29. Herding as a pasture-water-return circuit
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: A herd is sustained by managed alternation between release to pasture, movement to water, intake, and return to enclosure.
- Bridge: repeated husbandry scene and causal sequence; the shepherd guards, releases, and routes the animals, suitable pasture feeds them, watering interrupts grazing, and evening return closes the cycle.
- Active bridge motifs: cattle within the managed herd (`ب ق ر:B001/m01`); grazing ground (`ر ع ي:B001/m01`); guardianship by a shepherd (`ر ع ي:B002/m01`); release to pasture (`س ر ح:B005/m01`); night movement toward water (`ق ر ب:B008/m01`); watering at the animals' mouths (`ق ب ل:B014/m01`); alternation between water and pasture (`ن د و:B006/m01`); evening return to the pen (`ر و ح:B005/m01`); pasture suited to the herd (`و ص ي:B004/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P3 “Provision under bodily constraint”; P4 “Bovine traction and field work”; P14 “River crossing as a test of intake”.
- Synthesis: Pasture and water are not merely adjacent resources. Their managed alternation forms a complete husbandry circuit with a responsible keeper and a returning herd.

### X30. Horse prepared, accelerated, mounted, and tested
- Pericopes spanned: P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P5 (2:75-86), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P12 (2:204-220), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Mounted force emerges from fitting and controlling an animal, increasing its gait, and sustaining rider and mount under contest.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; tack makes riding possible, rein and gait regulate acceleration, marked or pastured horses are prepared, and steadiness converts speed into effective contest.
- Active bridge motifs: saddle girth beneath the mount (`ب ط ن:B006/m01`); riding a mount (`ر ك ب:B001/m01`); urging a horse by extending the rein (`ب ل غ:B007/m01`); controlled running gait (`ق ر ب:B014/m01`); full gallop (`ح ض ر:B004/m01`); horses released or prepared in pasture (`س و م:B003/m01`); advancing in a race (`س ب ق:B001/m01`); courage and steadiness under battle (`ث ب ت:B002/m01`).

- Shared semantic invariant: The hand controls material by changing configuration between open reach, measured scoop, closed possession, and release to another.
- Bridge: causal motor sequence with role progression; an open hand reaches or offers, a cupped hand measures, closure secures possession, and extension completes transfer.
- Active bridge motifs: open or extended hand (`ب س ط:B004/m01`); measured hand-scoop (`غ ر ف:B001/m01`); closing the palm on an object (`ق ب ض:B001/m01`); grip-point on a tool (`ق ب ض:B002/m01`); hand as transfer instrument (`ي د ي:B007/m01`); palm-to-palm contact (`ص ف ح:B004/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P5 “Acquisition, handover, and price”; P14 “River crossing as a test of intake”; P16 “Written, witnessed, and pledged transfer”.
- Synthesis: The bridge is a motor transformation of the same bodily tool. It excludes symbolic finger coding, which has a different operation and outcome in X51.

### X53. Patterned voice from answering line to verse and song
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P3 (2:40-61), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Voice becomes patterned performance when sound follows sound, returns as refrain, and is organized by line or measured division.
- Bridge: repeated performance signature and role progression; one singer follows another, recurring sound stabilizes melody, a verse gathers words under meter, and prosodic division makes the pattern reproducible.
- Active bridge motifs: one voice following another (`ت ل و:B007/m01`); repeated or returned vocal phrase (`ر ج ع:B007/m01`); pleasurable musical hearing (`س م ع:B007/m01`); singing voice (`غ ن ي:B003/m01`); metrical verse line (`ب ي ت:B003/m01`); composed poetry (`ش ع ر:B007/m01`); prosodic division of verse (`ق ط ع:B022/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P6 “Voiced relay”; P9 “Public transmission of known truth”; P11 “Speech delivered to its hearer”.
- Synthesis: This channel is defined by patterned vocal form, not communication in general. Sender, answering voice, recurrence, and meter produce a performance scene.

### X54. Amulet, knot, and recitation acting as a spell mechanism
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P6 (2:87-103), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: A spell is externalized through a prepared object, binding knot, or recited formula intended to restrain, redirect, or protect a person.
- Bridge: tool-and-operation assembly; amulet carries the intended protection, knot materializes binding, recitation activates the formula, and the claimed outcome is restraint, redirection, or defense.
- Active bridge motifs: hanging protective amulet (`ت م م:B002/m01`); protective charm or incantation (`ع و ذ:B002/m01`); spell that restrains a person (`ء خ ذ:B004/m01`); magical knot (`ع ق د:B013/m01`); recited protective formula (`ع ز م:B003/m01`); charm claimed to redirect the heart (`ص ر ف:B009/m01`); face-turning bead (`ق ب ل:B016/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P6 “Separation engineered into harm”; P13 “Knotted and released speech”.
- Synthesis: The bridge is a claimed mechanism joining object, binding operation, utterance, and intended effect. It remains distinct from ordinary contractual knots or spoken proof.

### X55. Fragrance applied, diffused, and recognized
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P2 (2:21-39), P3 (2:40-61), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P12 (2:204-220), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Fragrant material becomes perceptible by being prepared or applied, released into air, and identified through smell.
- Bridge: causal sensory sequence; perfume or camphor supplies material, application fixes it to body or cloth, diffusion creates odor, and olfactory recognition identifies its quality.
- Active bridge motifs: perfumed paste applied to a surface (`خ ل ق:B010/m01`); scented cosmetic and color (`خ م ر:B006/m01`); fragrant substance (`ط ي ب:B007/m01`); camphor perfume (`ك ف ر:B011/m01`); odor perceived by smell (`ر و ح:B004/m01`); scent recognized or used to perfume (`ع ر ف:B004/m01`).
- Synthesis: The channel follows one material-sensory process. Visual beauty and textile coloration remain separate unless scent is the active property.

### X56. Death passing into burial, grave, and estate
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P2 (2:21-39), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P13 (2:221-242), P14 (2:243-253), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: Death changes a person from living agent into a body concealed in a fixed dwelling and a predecessor who leaves property behind.
- Bridge: causal sequence and role progression; vital force ends, the body is covered and placed in a grave, the grave becomes a final house, and surviving goods become an estate for others.
- Active bridge motifs: loss of life (`م و ت:B001/m01`); death as release from toil (`ر و ح:B016/m01`); burial and concealment of the dead (`ج ن ن:B009/m01`); grave as a house (`ب ي ت:B007/m01`); final resting place (`ص ي ر:B007/m01`); grave secured for the dead (`ر ه ن:B006/m01`); estate left behind (`ت ر ك:B006/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P8 “Presence at the terminal moment”; P11 “Testament securing kin after death”; P14 “Life spared, taken, and evidenced”; P15 “Stillness, death, and return to life”.
- Synthesis: X9 concerns animation and revival; this channel follows the irreversible social and spatial consequences of death through burial and succession.

### X57. Illness passing through care into recovery
- Pericopes spanned: P1 (2:1-20), P3 (2:40-61), P4 (2:62-74), P5 (2:75-86), P6 (2:87-103), P7 (2:104-121), P8 (2:122-141), P9 (2:142-152), P10 (2:153-177), P11 (2:178-203), P12 (2:204-220), P13 (2:221-242), P15 (2:254-266), and P16 (2:267-286).
- Shared semantic invariant: A body departs from health, receives sustained care, and either relapses or returns toward sound condition.
- Bridge: causal sequence with outcome contrast; ailment establishes disequilibrium, care attends the patient, convalescence separates illness from the body, while relapse reverses improvement.
- Active bridge motifs: departure from bodily health (`م ر ض:B001/m01`); tending a patient (`م ر ض:B003/m01`); recovery from illness (`ب ر ء:B003/m01`); improvement after wasting (`ب ل ل:B003/m01`); illness departing the patient (`ف ر ق:B010/m01`); return toward health (`م ث ل:B012/m01`); relapse after improvement (`غ ف ر:B004/m01`); bodily safety from defect (`س ل م:B001/m01`).
- Local findings joined: P6 “Life-force entering and leaving the body”; P10 “Care distributed through the social body”; P15 “Stillness, death, and return to life”.
- Synthesis: Disease, care, recovery, and relapse form a medical trajectory. Wounds requiring probing or compensation remain in X19.
